objectives.name: Key Site
objectives.description: Nominate one Dropsite at least 24” from your Deployment Zone before the game. If you Control it at the end of the game, gain 2VP. If this Dropsite is within 6” or inside your opponent’s Deployment Zone, gain 3VP instead.

objectives.name: Priority Target
objectives.description: Nominate one Medium or Large Dropsite at least 24” from your Deployment Zone before the game. If you have Levelled it, at the end of the game gain 2VP. If this Dropsite is within 6” or inside your opponent’s Deployment zone, gain 3VP instead.

objectives.name: Long Shot
objectives.description: Nominate one Feature in a Dropsite within 12” of an opponent’s Deployment Zone before the game. If you have destroyed it, at the end of the game, gain 2VP. Each Feature can only be nominated once but a Dropsite can have more than one nominated Feature.

objectives.name: Annihilate
objectives.description: You are awarded 1VP at the end of the game for every 500 points of Ships and Admirals you have destroyed. A maximum of 3VP may be scored using this Secondary Objective.

objectives.name: Take Prizes
objectives.description: You are awarded 1VP at the end of the game for every 100 points of Ships you have captured. A maximum of 3VP may be scored using this Secondary Objective.

objectives.name: Gather Intel
objectives.description: You are awarded 1VP whenever you survey a Dropsite at least 24" away from your deployment zone. Any Capital Ship within 6” of the Dropsite and able to fire Weapons may substitute all attacking and launching that round to Survey it. Each Dropsite may be Surveyed once per player per game. A maximum of 2VP may be scored using this Secondary Objective. If the Scenario normally uses Survey, these VP are scored in addition to those in the Scenario.

objectives.name: Decapitate
objectives.description: You are awarded 2VP if you kill your opponent’s highest-Level Admiral (or one of if there are multiple with the same Level).

objectives.name: Objectives Beyond
objectives.description: Nominate one of your Ships of Tonnage M or higher. You may permanently fly that Ship off the board in any opponent’s Deployment Zone. If you do and that ship is not Crippled, gain 1VP. If that ship was H or C tonnage, gain 2VP instead.

Aegis-X.description:
All Ships with this rule in a Group combine their X values into a single value, Y.
Friendly Groups in coherency within 6” of a Ship with this rule and the same Orbital Layer (including its own Group) gain the benefits of Aegis.
When rolling saves against Close Action and Bomber (of any type) attacks, those Groups gain Y additional save dice they may add to those saves. Before rolling to save, the defending player assigns these dice against specific weapons, divided up as they choose (including any modified hits).
An Aegis Group can only grant the benefits of Aegis once each time a friendly group is attacked.
A friendly Group can only benefit from Aegis from one Group each time it is attacked.

Cloak-X.description: This Group may have a maximum of X Spikes.

Command Ship-X.description: Increase the Level of any Admiral assigned to this Ship by X.

Descent.description:
Ships with the Descent special rule are designed to work in Atmosphere and are referred to as Descent Ships, which may be part of Descent Groups. The atmospheric operational depth of these Ships is far lower than normal ships.
When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.
When attacking into Orbit from Atmosphere, any attack always hits on a 6+.
A non-Descent Ship that ends its activation in Atmosphere takes D3 damage. Colossal Ships take 2D3 damage instead.

Detector.description: If this Ship is on an order that allows it to attack, this Ship may forgo one allowed Weapon use during its activation. If it does, at the end of its activation place two Spikes on an enemy Group in line of sight. A Group that uses Detector gains a Spike (regardless of the amount of Ships using this rule).

Escort.description:
After Weapons have been assigned to a friendly Ship of H or C tonnage within 6” of this Ship on the same Orbital Layer, you may declare the use of Escort for the friendly Ship. Only one Group may Escort at a time and it must be in Coherency.
After your opponent rolls to hit the original target, allocate an amount of hits from that roll to this Group. An Escort Group cannot be allocated more damage by those hits than each remaining Ship in it has in starting Hull. You may use this even if the Escort Group is out of range, arc, and line of sight of the attacking Group. Continue the attack sequence using the Escort Group.
Weapons with the Focused rule cannot be affected by the Escort rule.

Gateship-X.description:
Shaltari Motherships must launch their Dropships via a Ship/Dropsite with this rule (sometimes referred to as Gateships). Each Gateship can have up to X Dropships deployed from it each round. Note: though the launch is measured from the Gateship, it is the Mothership that is launching.
When this Ship goes on the Weapons Free, Max Thrust, or Damage Control orders, it reduces its Gateship-X value to 0 until the start of its next activation.

Hero.description: You can only include two Groups with this special rule in your fleet. You cannot assign an Admiral to this Ship when building your fleet.

Impetuous.description: At the start of each round, friendly Groups with this rule improve the Lock of their Weapon Systems by 1 until you activate a friendly Group without this rule.

Marines-X.description: Remove X enemy Battalions from this Ship at the beginning of the Battalion Combat step.

Monitor.description: Ships with this rule may not use Course Change or Max Thrust orders.

Mothership.description: Shaltari Motherships can only deploy their Dropships via friendly Ships/Dropsites with the Gateship-X special rule (sometimes referred to as Gateships). These Gateships must be within 18” of the Mothership or part of a chain of Gateships with each Gateship in the chain being within 18” of another. Note: though the launch is measured from the Gateship, it is the Mothership that is launching.

Payload S/L-X.description:
When building your fleet, you may choose as many Payload Ships as you like— tonnage limits do not apply to these Ships, and they have no Group size. All Payload S/L Ships must be assigned to a Porter S/L Ship with the same letter. Payload Ships may not activate or be targeted until detached.
Payload Ships take up X of a Porter Ship’s capacity.
During the Porter Ship’s activation, if it is on an Order that allows it to Launch, you may detach one or more of its Payload Ships and place them within 3” of it. In the round they are detached, these Payloads activate together immediately as part of the Porter Ship’s activation after it has completed its Order. In subsequent rounds, all your Payload Ships count as being part of a single Group. Crippling Effects, Spikes, and other rules that affect an entire Group only affect the targeted Payload Ship.
Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.
If a Payload Ship is attached to a Porter Ship when that Ship is destroyed, the Payload Ship is destroyed.

Porter S/L-X.description:
This Ship may be assigned Payload Ships with the same letter up to a total capacity of X.
During a Porter’s activation, it may attach any detached Payload Ships within 3” if it has available capacity. Payload Ships reattached to a Porter Ship are removed from the table to be deployed in a later round.
Any tokens, Spikes, or effects affecting the reattached Payload Ship are removed from that Ship.

Rapid Drop.description: This Ship may launch its Assets at any point during its movement

Rare.description: You may only take one Group of this Ship in a Skirmish-sized game, two in a Clash, three in a Battle, and four in a Reconquest.

Regenerate-X.description: This Ship recovers X lost Hull Points at the end of its activation.

Reinforced Armour.description: Weapons rolling to hit this Ship or its Group can only score criticals against it on a result of a 3 higher than its Lock value.

Shield-X.description:
This Group has a Shield Save of X+. After Weapons have been assigned to this Group or Assets attack this Group, you may declare the use of Shield Saves for this Group. If you do, this Group replaces its Energy and Kinetic Saves with their Shield Saves for that attack sequence. Shield Saves can be used against Energy, Kinetic, and Core damage and ignore any modifiers to Energy and Kinetic Saves. Backup Saves may then be used after Shield Saves as normal.
A Group gains a single Spike each time it uses its Shield saves (regardless of the number of saves made per use).
Hits caused by Boarding Actions cannot be saved by Shield Saves.

Stealth.description: This Ship may fire one Weapon while Silent Running.

Unique.description: You may only take one Group of this Ship.

Vanguard-X.description: Groups with this rule may begin the game Directly Deployed, ignoring the normal Scenario Deployment and Approach Types (though still counting towards Groups Directly Deployed). If it does, it may be deployed up to X” away from your Deployment Zone.

Vectored.description: This Ship may make an additional turn at any point during its movement, regardless of the Order its Group has taken.

Air to Air.description: This weapon ignores the penalties for attacking Ships in Atmosphere while the attacking Ship is also in Atmosphere.

Alt-X.description:
Only one Weapon or Load with the same Alt value on the same Ship may be used by that Ship each round.
All Alt Weapons with the same value count as the same Weapon when determining how many Weapons a Ship has.

Alt Launch.description: In a round this Weapon is fired this Ship may not launch Assets.

Anti Wing.description: This weapon may target enemy Wings as if they were Ships (with a Sig of 0”) but reduces its Lock value by 1 for that attack. If it does, for each hit, remove 1 Fighter or 1 Bomber from that Wing or any other enemy Wing within 3” of the target.

Arrest-X.description: A Ship damaged by this Weapon reduces its Thrust by X” during its next activation. A Ship can only be affected by this rule once each round.

Bloom-X.description: Whenever you fire this Weapon (including separate attacks generated by the Volley-X special rule), the attacking Group gains X Spikes.

Bombardment.description:
This Weapon ignores the penalties for attacking Cities and Ships in Atmosphere.
Improve the Lock of this Weapon by 2 when attacking Cities.
When attacking a Ship in Orbit with this weapon, it always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
This weapon cannot be used to attack Ships in Orbit while the attacking Ship is in Atmosphere.

Burnthrough-X.description: Each of this Weapon’s critical hits reduces the target’s Energy/Kinetic Save by X for hits caused by this Weapon for this attack. Saves made for other Weapons are unaffected. Roll attacks separately for each Burnthrough Weapon.

Calibre-X.description: Improve the Lock value of this Weapon by 1 when attacking Groups of any of the listed X Tonnage values.

Close Action.description: This Weapon may only be fired at targets within Scan range and on the same Orbital Layer as the attacking Ship.

Close Protection.description: After rolling Kinetic or Energy saves against Close Action and Bomber (of any type) attacks, you may declare the use of any number of Fighters. Each Fighter used confers its re-rolls to a defending friendly Group within its Thrust range. The defending player assigns all re-rolls from each Fighter against specific weapons, dividing up Fighters as they choose. Shield and Backup saves cannot be re-rolled this way. Once a Fighter has been used in this way, remove it.

Corruptor-X.description: When this Weapon successfully inflicts damage, place X Battalions on the target.

Crippling-X.description: If an attack from this Weapon scores at least one Critical hit and then damages a Ship (following normal damage allocation rules), the damaged Ship gains the stated X Crippling Effect regardless of Tonnage. If no effect is listed, roll 2D6 and apply the corresponding Crippling Effect from the table.

Crippling-Fire.description: If an attack from this Weapon scores at least one Critical hit and then damages a Ship (following normal damage allocation rules), the damaged Ship gains this Crippling Effect regardless of Tonnage (in addition to any Crippling Effect from being reduced below half Hull). Fire: Gain a Fire Token. At the start of the End Phase, before the Repair step, this Ship suffers a point of damage for each Fire Token it has. Repairable.

Crippling-2xFire.description: If an attack from this Weapon scores at least one Critical hit and then damages a Ship (following normal damage allocation rules), the damaged Ship gains this Crippling Effect regardless of Tonnage (in addition to any Crippling Effect from being reduced below half Hull). Gain two Fire Tokens (Fire is the one Crippling Effect a Ship may hold more than one of). At the start of the End Phase, before the Repair step, this Ship suffers a point of damage for each Fire Token it has. Repairable.

Crippling-Navigation Offline.description: If an attack from this Weapon scores at least one Critical hit and then damages a Ship (following normal damage allocation rules), the damaged Ship gains this Crippling Effect regardless of Tonnage (in addition to any Crippling Effect from being reduced below half Hull). Navigation Offline: Gain a Navigation Offline token, reducing this Ship’s total movement to 2” (regardless of Thrust) and preventing it from turning or changing Orbital Layer. Repairable.

Crippling-Weapons Offline.description: If an attack from this Weapon scores at least one Critical hit and then damages a Ship (following normal damage allocation rules), the damaged Ship gains this Crippling Effect regardless of Tonnage (in addition to any Crippling Effect from being reduced below half Hull). Weapons Offline: Gain a Weapons Offline token, preventing this Ship from using Weapons or launching Assets. Repairable.

Critical-X.description: Each of this Weapon’s criticals increases the damage of that hit by X.

Escape Velocity.description:
This weapon ignores the penalty for attacking Ships in Orbit and treats all Ships in Atmosphere as non-Descent Ships, so only reduces its Lock by 1 when attacking Ships in Atmosphere.
Close Action weapons with this special rule may be used against targets in Orbit while the attacking Ship is in Atmosphere.

Flash-X.description: When this Weapon inflicts damage, the damaged Group (or Ship if it ignores the usual coherency rules) gains X Spikes.

Focused.description:
Instead of the normal potential targets for Weapons, this Weapon’s potential targets are either:
• A single enemy Ship.
• A Dropsite containing no friendly Battalions.
Damage caused by this Weapon is allocated to only the target.

Fusillade-X.description: This Weapon increases its Attack value by X while its Ship is on Weapons Free.

High Power.description:
Unless the attacking Ship is on the Weapons Free Order, attacking with this Weapon counts as attacking with two Weapons (though it only fires once).
Ships with only a single High Power Weapon can only attack with it while on the Weapons Free Order.

Impel-X.description:
If an attacking Group scores at least X critical hits with this Weapon System against a Group, choose one of the following for each affected Group:
A) Turn all Ships in that Group 45 degrees in the same direction. If the Group scored at least twice X, turn all Ships in that Group 90 degrees in the same direction instead.
B) Move all Ships in that Group up to twice X inches directly forward (measuring from the affected Ships). Ships moved this way cannot be moved into Large Objects or off of the table.
A Group can only be affected by each effect once per Weapon System per attack sequence.

Limited-X.description:
This Weapon can only be fired X times per game.
You may launch a total of X of this Asset per game.

Linked-X.description: Weapons with the same Linked-X value on the same Ship count as 1 Weapon for Orders purposes. When you attack with a Linked-X Weapon, you attack with all other Weapons on that Ship with the same Linked-X value.

Low Power.description: If a Ship’s Orders allow it to fire Close Action Weapons, it may attack with one Low Power Weapon in addition to any other Weapons allowed by its Order.

Mauler.description: The Lock value of this Weapon is equal to the save the target would use to defend against it.

Overcharge.description: Before assigning Weapons to targets, you may double the Damage value of this Weapon. If you do, this becomes a High Power Weapon for this activation and each attack roll of 6 causes that attacking Ship to lose this Weapon’s unmodified Damage value in hull points. Only one Weapon per Ship may benefit from this rule per activation.

Penetrator.description: Each of this Weapon’s critical hits cause a Core hit instead of its normal Damage Type.

Re-Entry.description:
This weapon ignores the penalties for attacking Ships in Atmosphere while the attacking Ship is in Orbit.
Close Action weapons with this special rule may be used against targets in Atmosphere while the attacking Ship is in Orbit.

Reave-X.description: Each of this Weapon’s criticals reduces the Energy/Kinetic save used against that hit by X.

Scald-X.description: If this weapon attacks a target within Scan range, reduce the target’s Energy / Kinetic save against this weapon's hits by X (other attacks and Weapons are unaffected).

Status.description:
When you hit with this Weapon, pick one of the following tokens; Defence Systems Offline, Scanners Offline, or Navigation Offline. 
At the end of the Inflict Damage step, choose one of the defending Ships to gain the selected token, regardless of the amount of damage caused by the attack or amount of hits saved. This token is automatically removed at the start of the End Phase, before making repairs.

Sustained Fire.description: If this Weapon attacks a target Group it hit in the previous round, double its Attack value for this attack.

Volley-X.description:
This Weapon counts as 1 Weapon for Orders purposes. When you assign this Weapon to a target, you assign it to targets up to X times (either the same or different). Once assigned, treat each allocation as a separate weapon for the subsequent steps in the attack sequence.
Broadside Weapons using Volley must alternate arcs when determining and assigning targets (so cannot target the same Group on the same side twice in a row).

Crippling.description: If an attack from this Weapon scores at least one Critical hit and then damages a Ship (following normal damage allocation rules), the damaged Ship suffers a Crippling Effect regardless of Tonnage: roll 2D6 and apply the result from the Crippling Effect table.

options.name: Deep Space Tracking
options.effect: When this Space Station targets enemy ships, Spikes on those ships have double their normal effect. So a Spike would increase the target's Signature by 6" instead of 3".

options.name: Scanner Uplink
options.effect: This Space Station's Scan range is increased by 3". In addition, friendly ships within 3" of one or more Space Stations with this special rule increase their Scan range by 3". This special rule ceases to function while this Space Station is controlled by an enemy player.

options.name: Astrobotanical Lab
options.subtitle: Exo-Greenhouse
options.effect: Signature Bloom: Friendly Ships within this Space Station's unmodified Signature are Hidden within its Bloom. Enemy Ships targeting a Hidden Ship's Group ignore a Spike for each Hidden Ship in that Group. This rule has no effect while this Space Station is controlled by an enemy player.

abilities.name: Backpedal
abilities.effect: At the start of a friendly Group’s activation, pick any friendly Group. You may move each Ship in that Group up to 3” directly backwards.

abilities.name: Gravitic Manoeuvring
abilities.effect: When a friendly Group is given a Max Thrust Order, it may turn as if it was on General Quarters.

abilities.name: Kinetic Deconstruction
abilities.effect: When a friendly Group makes an attack with any number of weapons with “Decon” in its name, those weapons change their Type to Kinetic until the end of its activation.

abilities.name: Overwatch
abilities.effect: When you activate this Ship on General Quarters, you may choose to forgo attacking with this Ship. If you do, this Ship goes on Overwatch until the end of the round or until it declares the use of Overwatch. At the end of any enemy Group’s activation, if that Group moved through this Ship’s Front arc and was in weapons range while doing so, you may declare the use of Overwatch against that Group. When you use Overwatch, this Ship immediately makes an Attack as if on General Quarters against the enemy Group, even if it is out of arc and weapon range.

ship.lore: In 2679, the Zenith class Bioficer dreadnought is the most dreaded close-action vessel in known space. In several early engagements with admirals who didn’t appreciate what they were facing, a single example chewed through scores of capital ships and emerged victorious. The Zenith’s primary prow armament is the Giga Lightvice. This weapon’s fanged maw emits a biblical level of atomic destruction capable of rending a battleship in seconds. Like its cousin the Zodiac, the Zenith’s prow-ventral hardpoint will accept any battleship primary armament, although on a dreadnought this is merely secondary. Tertiary armament is typically a quad array of Thermators, another weapon which does its killing up close. Completing the Zenith’s offensive suite is a substantial, exposed spinal flight deck. Reporting class: Dreadnought. Every Dreadnought carries a designation beginning with Z.

Giga Lightvice When determining potential targets for this weapon, you may use an unmodifiable Scan of 7” instead of this Ship’s Scan value. ship.lore: The Zodiac is the most frequently encountered Bioficer dreadnoughts, although all sightings are thankfully rare, so far. These hellish leviathans pack an array of ship-killing weapons, starting with a pair of Decon Annihilators. Moving downwards, a secondary hardpoint will accept any battleship primary armament as a secondary aboard this monster. Towards the stern is typically a quad battery of Scythes. Lastly, a spinal flight deck is open to the void, ready to unleash waves of lethal bombers or nimble fighters. Nothing less than another dreadnought can hope to survive an encounter with this monster. Reporting class: Dreadnought. Every Dreadnought carries a designation beginning with Z.

ship.lore: Consistent with the enemy's other super battleships, the Binder is effectively an up-gunned, slower derivative of the Bastion class. Its devastating, mixed armament is a primary threat to any vessel. Like other Bioficer super battleships, it features a greater offensive crew compliment to fill its boarding pods, making boarding actions against this leviathan a foolhardy endeavour. ship.lore: The Brutal class battleship is built around the terrifying Giga-Winnower, a weapon of awesome, indiscriminate lethality. variants.name: Styx
variants.lore:
Although all Bioficer sightings are rare, if increasing, certain ship classes have only been observed once. The sole record of the fearsome Styx class comes from the mangled tertiary flight recorder of the battleship UCMS Bellaque. She was lost with all hands in the Eden system, and only an atomic cloud and cored-out hull fragments remained – the work of the fearsome Decon Annihilator, the Styx’s colossal primary weapon.

The Styx seems to have similar capabilities to the Stature class, but utilises an enlarged, novel hull more closely related to Bioficer cruisers. Some believe this vessel was unique, casting further doubt on the old notion that the Bioficers lack individuality.

variants.lore: The Anomaly is an anomalous starship sighted on the battlefields of the Reconquest, with almost nothing known of its allegiances, specifications, or capabilities. The ship is said to be capable of moving at beyond-relativistic speeds while in realspace. No life signs were detected aboard by UCM scans, yet the presence of unusually homogeneous organic matter has been revealed through spectral analysis. Though the Anomaly's hull is substantially different from that of known Bioficer vessels, it carries the same armament as a Construct-class cruiser, hinting that it may be an alternative form of that ship.

ship.lore: Nicknamed by lucky survivors, The Melter became a feared lone wolf among Bioficer raiding parties. Its favoured victims were larger foes who didn’t feel as threatened by a vessel of its modest size as they should. No other ship was known in this configuration, so the Admiralty assigned its guiding Intelligence the designation Anode. This individual was entirely unsubtle and clearly had access to superior technology over its peers. It featured an enhanced superstructure and power matrix, upping it to heavy destroyer tonnage. All this supported a single, prow weapons system: the Themator Cage. Quite different in form to regular thermators, this was as devastating as most battleship primary armaments, albeit only at close range. This led to the vessel’s destruction at the hands of the UCMS Gaugamela over Olympus in early 2679. However, reports of an identical vessel and characteristic behaviours followed weeks later, forcing the Admiralty to conclude that this Intelligence had successfully transferred out and potentially has several of these unusual vessels at its disposal.

When attacking into Orbit from Atmosphere, any attack always hits on a 6+.

specialRules.name: Payload L-1
specialRules.description:
When building your fleet, you may choose as many Payload Ships as you like— tonnage limits do not apply to these Ships, and they have no Group size. All Payload S/L Ships must be assigned to a Porter S/L Ship with the same letter. Payload Ships may not activate or be targeted until detached.
Payload Ships take up 1 of a Porter Ship’s capacity.
During the Porter Ship’s activation, if it is on an Order that allows it to Launch, you may detach one or more of its Payload Ships and place them within 3” of it. In the round they are detached, these Payloads activate together immediately as part of the Porter Ship’s activation after it has completed its Order. In subsequent rounds, all your Payload Ships count as being part of a single Group. Crippling Effects, Spikes, and other rules that affect an entire Group only affect the targeted Payload Ship.
Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.
If a Payload Ship is attached to a Porter Ship when that Ship is destroyed, the Payload Ship is destroyed.

specialRules.name: Aegis-3
specialRules.description:
All Ships with this rule in a Group combine their 3 values into a single value, Y.
Friendly Groups in coherency within 6” of a Ship with this rule and the same Orbital Layer (including its own Group) gain the benefits of Aegis.
When rolling saves against Close Action and Bomber (of any type) attacks, those Groups gain Y additional save dice they may add to those saves. Before rolling to save, the defending player assigns these dice against specific weapons, divided up as they choose (including any modified hits).

A Ship with this rule cannot gain the benefit of Aegis from another Ship with this rule.

specialRules.name: Payload S-1
specialRules.description:
When building your fleet, you may choose as many Payload Ships as you like— tonnage limits do not apply to these Ships, and they have no Group size. All Payload S/L Ships must be assigned to a Porter S/L Ship with the same letter. Payload Ships may not activate or be targeted until detached.
Payload Ships take up 1 of a Porter Ship’s capacity.
During the Porter Ship’s activation, if it is on an Order that allows it to Launch, you may detach one or more of its Payload Ships and place them within 3” of it. In the round they are detached, these Payloads activate together immediately as part of the Porter Ship’s activation after it has completed its Order. In subsequent rounds, all your Payload Ships count as being part of a single Group. Crippling Effects, Spikes, and other rules that affect an entire Group only affect the targeted Payload Ship.
Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.
If a Payload Ship is attached to a Porter Ship when that Ship is destroyed, the Payload Ship is destroyed.

specialRules.name: Subservient Mercenaries
specialRules.description: Pungari Threshers may be used in any fleet but always use Shaltari Fire Ships. When used in a Shaltari fleet, this Ship gains Shield-5+.

ship.lore:
The UCM first encountered the Pungari as part of a Shaltari force during Phase 2 of the Reconquest. Unlike their masters, they were prolific in numbers. In them, the Shaltari found a subservient race to exploit in much the same way they had planned for humanity.

Sightings of Pungari ships were reported shortly afterwards, not all had fallen in with the Shaltari. Apparently, the Pungari are new to starfaring; their blocky ships are primitive yet robust. Instead of the low-crew, high-firepower approach advanced generators afford to other races, the Pungari leverage sheer numbers. Routinely, they hurl thousands into suicidal boarding actions; something Pungari do willingly and, as far as UCM soldiers can tell, with much glee. Their stocky frames may cope with the extreme g-forces involved, unencumbered by too much brain to damage.

When encountering Pungari it is always a coin toss on whether they attack or not. They may try to broker simple alliances, happy to plunge into the wars of other races without expecting much in return, beyond a master to serve in awe.

ship.name: Hyperyacht Aurorum

specialRules.name: Marines-2
specialRules.description: Remove 2 enemy Battalions from this Ship at the beginning of the Battalion Combat step.

specialRules.name: Stealth
specialRules.description: This Ship may fire one Weapon while Silent Running.

specialRules.name: Unique
specialRules.description: You may only take one Group of this Ship.

ship.lore:
Hyperyacht Aurorum, launched 2493, was commissioned by Caesar Dun, boss of the East Eden Syndicate. She was uniquely built to impeccable standards, riddled with unregistered spaces, and armed far beyond EAA-sanctioned levels. While using her peerless stealth capabilities to evade justice, he unwittingly dodged the Scourge invasion. After months of shadowing a survivor flotilla, Caesar was garrotted by his lieutenant, who took Aurorum to join the refugees.

Today, Aurorum serves as the flagship of Karl Stieglitz, head of the galaxy's most infamous mercenaries: The Decapitators. This privateer flotilla earned dark renown during the Battle of Earth in the vanguard of the Vega Scrapfleet but is now a gun for hire. Stieglitz has already been approached by Kalium and, it is rumoured, the PHR. The UCM has yet to decide how to respond.

ship.name: Hyperyacht Somniferum

specialRules.name: Unique
specialRules.description: You may only take one Group of this Ship.

ship.lore:
The Hyperyacht Somniferum is not a sight civilized governments want to see on situation reports. Colloquially known as "the party bus", a spike in crime and illegal substances usually follows in its wake. Somniferum's current owner is the "Master of Ceremonies" Maeby Hy. The Somniferum is almost unrecognisable from its initial configuration as an Eden Aerospace Systems Luxury Liner. Lab explosions, combat damage, and ad-hoc refits have all added to it's hodge-podge appearance.

One of these many changes to the ship is the addition of a peculiar weapon system. While it has no official name, the crew and any who face it have dubbed it "Party Poppers". This weapon system fires armour piercing fragmenting flechettes that disperse airborne narcotics and electromagnetic interference into its target. Far too small and numerous to effectively track, this weapon is able to bypass the majority of a ship's point defences and deliver strikes straight to the hull.

The Somniferum is rarely seen over combat zones, preferring to stick to those planets that are safe enough for civilian travel. While able to defend itself against small time competitors, the ship isn't built for combat. More often than not, the Somniferum will make a hasty exit from a planet as soon as it detects any law enforcement on an intercept course.

ship.name: LKS Dredger

specialRules.name: Industrial Design
specialRules.description: Improve this Group’s Backup save by 2 when rolling to save hits due to Debris Fields.

ship.lore:
A relentless machine of industry, built to mulch, sift, and extract until its timer runs dry. It drills deep, rips apart rock, and spits out raw profit, indifferent to the hands that keep it running. No legacy, no ownership, just a contract ticking toward expiration. When time is up, it moves on, leaving its crew behind, waiting for the next company to stake its claim on the battered frame. Inside, the workers endure the constant grind, wedged between failing systems and the unyielding demand for productivity. Comfort is non-existent, maintenance is endless.

Equipped with a heavy duty drill and front mounted mining array, this vessel doesn't just extract minerals, it carves deep trenches into asteroid surfaces and space debris, kicking up clouds of pulverized rock and metallic sediment. A network of sediment filters and gravity sifting tanks separates valuable ore from dust before storing the processed materials in its cargo bays.

Prominently displayed on the ship's exterior, the countdown display isn't a warning, it's a fact. The contract will expire, and if it doesn't get topped up, the vessel moves on to whatever comes next. Passed from one mining company to the next, these hand me down workhorses run until their rental contracts dry up. Refurbished just enough to stay functional, they degrade with every transfer, patched, battered, barely space worthy, considered scrap with engines.

Upper management doesn't care about the ship, only the ore it pulls in before time runs out. The crew works under relentless pressure, knowing there's no guarantee of renewal.

When the timer hits zero, it's out of their hands. Either the contract gets extended, or the ship moves on.

Despite its size, the colossal vessel remains a world of tight corridors for its 190 crew members. Dust and grime clings to every surface, settling in forgotten corners and coating equipment in a fine greasy layer. Minimal comforts, constant maintenance, and the daily expectation that something will break.

ship.name: SLM-9 Resupply Hauler

specialRules.name: Vectored
specialRules.description: This Ship may make an additional turn at any point during its movement, regardless of the Order its Group has taken.

specialRules.name: Resupply and Rearm
specialRules.description:
If this ship ends its movement in base contact with a friendly ship of Medium Tonnage or higher or a Space Station, pick one of the following:
Resupply: That Ship or Space Station recovers 3 Hull points and remove any Crippling Effect tokens.
Rearm: Increase the Limited-X value of any of that Ship or Space Station's Weapons and Launch Assets by 1 until the end of the round.

specialRules.name: Flawed Design
specialRules.description: This Ship cannot use its Resupply and Rearm rule if it is below half of its starting Hull.

specialRules.name: Mercenary
specialRules.description: This Ship may be used in any Fleet regardless of faction. When taken as part of your fleet, this Ship loses its Boardable rule.

ship.lore:
A relic from the now liquidated Eden Void Logistics inc, the SLM-9 is a battle tested bulk logistics vessel, trusted for fleet replenishment in high risk environments. Though the company behind its design has since shuttered, the SLM-9 endures as a testament to their engineering prowess and affordability. Its metal cargo frame, hydraulic deployment arms and universal clamps ensure rapid, adaptable resupply of ordnance, fuel, and supplies anywhere. Rugged and inexpensive, the SLM-9 remains a reasonable choice for fleets needing a dependable workhorse at a fraction of the cost of newer models.

Unlike conventional Logistics Vessels that unload cargo gradually, the SLM-9 releases its entire payload in a single, controlled operation. Hydraulic deployment arms manoeuvre the entire cargo bed outward, allowing for structured and efficient transfer without manual unloading.

Built for adaptability, the SLM-9's pincer like grappling arms latch onto ships regardless of docking compatibility. Variable force actuators fine tune pressure, securing a stable hold without compromising hull integrity. Whether resupplying warships or assisting stranded vessels, its clamps ensure critical cargo transfer under any conditions.

The SLM-9's hydraulic deployment arms are its defining feature, but also its greatest liability. If compromised by enemy fire or mechanical failure, the vessel loses its ability to unload cargo entirely, rendering it useless. A damaged deployment system means supplies remain trapped onboard, preventing fleet resupply and turning the ship into dead weight. While reinforced plating offers some protection, direct hits can buckle the arms, leading to catastrophic failure.

Due to its critical vulnerability, the SLM-9 has begun to be phased out in favour of newer resupply haulers with reinforced unloading mechanisms and modular backup systems. The remaining SLM-9 units are considered outdated relics, still operational but increasingly rare.

ship.name: T-Type Tugboat

specialRules.name: Descent
specialRules.description:
When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.
When attacking into Orbit from Atmosphere, any attack always hits on a 6+.
A non-Descent Ship that ends its activation in Atmosphere takes D3 damage. Colossal Ships take 2D3 damage instead.

specialRules.description: If this Ship is on General Quarters and in base contact with another Ship (friendly or enemy) you may have it Tug that Ship instead of moving normally. If you do, this Ship may turn as normal but only moves up to 3”. The other Ship is then moved the same distance in the same direction, retaining its original facing. Ships can only be tugged this way up to a maximum of 6” each round.

ship.lore:
The T-Type was once a common sight across many shipyards. Due to the size of many pre-war ships, a way of moving these gargantuan vessels out of drydock was needed. T-Types were devised to be the answer to this sizeable problem. The first batch of these floated out of the assembly lines prior to the first Pathfinder, ready and waiting to guide it to a safe launching point. Since then, countless multitudes of these ships have been constructed. Most serve their entire service life in the void, however some are refitted as lunar landers once their superstructure becomes unusable for its intended purpose.

Only a small amount of these were refit with foldspace drives, the majority were only designed to work around a single planet and its satellites. Those that were refit tend to be found in independent fleets, where they assist in swapping components on their larger vessels. T-Types are not built for any form of combat, though their internal bracing gives them a certain resilience, they are unable to weather any attack from dedicated combat ships.

Some T-Types have been converted to function similarly to mines, albeit with a much more personal weapon system. These have weaponised their towing ability, captains with a death wish will attach their tug to an enemy vessel and set their engines to full. When performed right, this can violently tear vessels in half, though at the cost of the tugboat and its crew.

specialRules.name: Penal Legions
specialRules.description: When taken as part of your fleet, this Ship starts the game with 2 friendly Battalions on it. When any number of enemy Battalions are removed due to Boarding Actions or Battalion Combat on a Space Station within 6” of this Ship, place a single friendly Battalion on this Ship. This Ship’s Boarding Pods and Drop Pods can only be used while it has friendly Battalions on it and each Boarding Pod or Drop Pod launched causes one friendly Battalion on this Ship to be removed.

ship.lore:
The DH-Type represents one of the Colonial Fleet's largest run of dedicated long-range prison ships, built around a standardized architecture of reinforced armour, multi-tier detention decks and automated security. Originally intended strictly for high-risk inmate transport and remote incarceration, wartime pressures pushed the class into broader operational roles.

Though designed with consistent core systems, such as compartmentalized containment blocks, automated defensive suites, ECM shielding, and a C.A.G.E emitter field. The ships grew increasingly variable due to differing missions, retrofits, and partial deactivations. Although uncommon, Individual DH-Type vessels gained their own notoriety, such as Iron Veil, Remnant Forge, Dreadhold and Bright Spire. The DH-Type ships illustrated the evolution through conversions into troop transports, logistics carriers, medical ships, and frontier support platforms, often retaining traces of their original penal infrastructure.

In modern service, L1-class hulls endure as adaptable, if austere, multi-role assets. Their durable construction, intimidating infrastructure, and legacy security systems continue to define their operational character, reflecting both the robustness of the original design and the fleet's ongoing need to repurpose coercive architecture for broader demands.

ship.name: M-Type Barge

ship.lore:
M-Type Barges are the larger cousin of the L-Type. Produced at the same Tharsis Manufacturing shipyards over Mars, the M-Type was designed for corporate bulk shipping. Many and more of these were owned and operated by the enduring shipping companies of old Earth, each of them emblazoned with corporate livery. Designed and built after the L-Type, these ships feature much improved Foldspace drives as well as the latest innovations in structural bracing. Optimisations in production brought the build time on these freight behemoths down to only twice that of the L-Type.

Many of these were spared the events of the Scourge invasion, most would have been slowly moving between the colonies and the cradle worlds, far enough away to make emergency jumps to safety. The initial trade and logistics network of the UCM was built upon the backs of the M-Type, their reliability and availability gave the colonies enough trade stability to recover from the loss of the cradle worlds. M-Types are surprisingly rare in Resistance fleets, most of the captains of these ships were more interested in meeting deadlines and quotas than in doomsday predictions prior to the battle of Vega. Kalium is yet to be seen operating these ships, preferring the L-Type for combat resupply, though may potentially be using M-Types in more secure Kalium controlled systems.

Recent developments in prefabricated defensive structures have allowed a small number of these ships to carry deployable missile defence outposts in place of their normal cargo compliment. These outposts are designed to grant a foothold on a planet and supplement its missile halo while more permanent structures are built, re-purposed, or captured.

ship.lore: The Oblivion OBV64 Barge is a heavily armoured civilian vessel designed to transport extremely hazardous materials, unstable technology, failed reactors, and biohazards, too dangerous to store on planets. These ships travel discreetly between remote depots, derelict battlefields, and disposal zones. Crewed by an extensive team of highly trained specialists under strict quarantine and secrecy protocols, The Oblivion barge handles cargo that is often poorly understood or classified. Their role is to quietly remove dangerous discoveries and remnants from circulation before they can threaten the wider fleet, or attract unwanted attention.

Scrappy Plating: One friendly Ship within 6" recovers lost Hull points equal to the amount of scrap tokens removed.
Bodge Repairs: Remove a crippling effect from a friendly Ship within 6" for each scrap token removed.

ship.lore:
The Type-87 Terminus Harvester is a colossal reclamation vessel built to consume the unrepairable wreckage of war. Its monolithic maw engulfs chunks up to frigate tonnage, feeding them into vast crushing chambers where superheated hydraulic presses obliterate hull plating to slag. Two VX-22 Flensers detach from its hull, peeling derelicts apart and hauling scraps to their final destruction. Ancient, slow-moving, and relentless, it labours, stripping vessels down to raw material. Within its corroded halls, life is harsh. Dim corridors reek of burning metal as air filters struggle against decades of industrial smog.

The Type-87's wedge-like prow is battered and scarred, worn from decades of grinding through wreckage. Deep gouges and warped plating mark where debris crumpled beneath its relentless push, clearing the way for the behemoth behind.

A monolithic opening capable of engulfing entire frigates, feeding them into a crushing chamber spanning the volume of a megastructure. Inside, reinforced walls lined with titanic hydraulic presses grind vessels down in a superheated maelstrom of pulverized metal, reducing all to molten slag.

Equipped with two VX-22 Flensers, these small salvage vessels dock onto the Harvester's hull when idle but detach to roam wreckage fields. They Brutally peel derelicts apart piecemeal while hauling fragmented components to the crushing maw. Though technically separate, they operate as an extension of the Harvester, ensuring no usable scrap escapes consumption.

Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.

ship.lore:
The VX-22 Flensers are compact salvage vessels designed for brutal ship dismantling. Their prow mounted sawblades don't cut cleanly, they tear, shred, and rip through wreckage with unrestrained violence. Designed for aggressive reclamation, they are the smaller, more aggressive sibling to the T-Type Tugboat. Where the Tugboat manoeuvres and stabilizes wreckage for controlled processing, the Flensers gut derelicts with reckless brutality, prioritizing destruction over precision.

Heavy rotating saws brutally cut through hull plating, breaking it into manageable pieces and scattering debris as they progress. Instead of delicate incision, the Flensers' sawblades operate at maximum torque, chewing through reinforced bulkheads with enough force to buckle surrounding structure.

Their cutting mechanisms frequently overheat, causing violent energy surges that make their hulls shudder mid operation.

The Flenser hurls debris into the Type-87 Terminus Harvester's compactor bay, sometimes suffering brutal kickback as the churning machinery spits chunks back out. When it happens, the debris slams into its failing frame, worsening the damage and making every load a gamble.

Positioned below the cockpit, this reinforced plating shields pilots from wreckage kicked up during cutting operations. Sloped for maximum deflection, it redirects debris that could slam into the hull with deadly force, absorbing impacts before they buckle metal or breach compartments.

ship.name: PRK-91 Provenance Ark

specialRules.name: Genesis Spikes
specialRules.description: When this weapon successfully inflicts any amount of damage against a City, place a Mutant Fauna token on that Dropsite. Mutant Fauna tokens are not Battalions and cannot control or contest a Dropsite. When any player deploys any number of Battalions to that Dropsite, if that Dropsite has any Mutant Fauna tokens, those Battalions are only placed on a roll of a 5+. If any Battalions are not placed this way, remove a Mutant Fauna token from that Dropsite. If a Dropsite starts a round with a Mutant Fauna token, remove that token at the end of the round.

specialRules.name: Expansive Radiator Systems
specialRules.description: At the start of this Ship's activation, remove two Spikes from it.

specialRules.name: Mercenary
specialRules.description: This Ship may be used in any Fleet regardless of faction. When taken as part of your fleet, this Ship loses its Boardable and Civilian Transport rules. This ship's Fighters & Bombers use the stats of its parent fleet (if you included this ship in a Scourge fleet, its Fighters & Bombers would follow the Scourge Fighters & Bombers rules).

ship.lore:
A monolithic vessel of unimaginable scale, the Provenance Ark dwarfs most ships. A precursor to the modular construction found on Coloniser class vessels, these ships were a talisman of hope and expansionism. These are the first major terraforming vessels built by mankind, reaching out into an unknown universe. Built to prepare entire worlds for habitation, it carries vast stores of genetic material, atmospheric stabilizers, and autonomous resource systems. The Ark monitors planetary progress through an extensive network of sensors and automated regulators, adjusting atmospheric composition, maintaining microbial balance, and even modulating gravitational and magnetic fields to stabilize emerging terrains.

Entire cities once mere schematics, rise, with power grids, transport arteries, and habitation modules ready long before the first settlers arrive. Inside, Construction drones and biotic cultivators orchestrate the birth of forests, oceans, and breathable atmospheres with the precision of a master artisan.

Many ships of this class feature underslung terraforming torpedo launchers. While near useless in ship to ship combat, these torpedoes are geared towards atmospheric re-entry and contain a plethora of mutagens and nerve agents, some of which would be used on Senator class battlecruisers. Under normal circumstances the use of these would constitute a war crime. Here they are simply used to rid prospective landing areas of their megafauna, causing mass hysteria and aggression in local fauna. Any issues with unruly creatures take care of themselves, and those left over can be cut down by specialised anti-fauna vehicles. Once the LZ is cleared of hostiles, the terraformer can then deploy more traditional terraforming methods.

specialRules.name: Feature Carrier
specialRules.description: At the start of the game, before players deploy, choose from the Gravitational Arc or Ghost Orb Tower Deployable Feature. This Ship starts the game carrying the chosen Deployable Feature.

stats.special: Vanguard-6", High Velocity Boarding Pods, Bombardment Spine

specialRules.name: Payload S-1
specialRules.description:
When building your fleet, you may choose as many Payload Ships as you like— tonnage limits do not apply to these Ships, and they have no Group size. All Payload S/L Ships must be assigned to a Porter S/L Ship with the same letter. Payload Ships may not activate or be targeted until detached.
Payload Ships take up 1 of a Porter Ship’s capacity.
During the Porter Ship’s activation, if it is on an Order that allows it to Launch, you may detach one or more of its Payload Ships and place them within 3” of it. In the round they are detached, these Payloads activate together immediately as part of the Porter Ship’s activation after it has completed its Order. In subsequent rounds, all your Payload Ships count as being part of a single Group. Crippling Effects, Spikes, and other rules that affect an entire Group only affect the targeted Payload Ship.
Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.
If a Payload Ship is attached to a Porter Ship when that Ship is destroyed, the Payload Ship is destroyed.

specialRules.name: Genitor Tower
specialRules.description: This Feature may be purchased for your fleet when you build your list. It must be assigned to a Ship with the Porter special rule as if it were a Ship with the Payload S-1 special rule. When one or more enemy Battalions on this Dropsite and its Features are removed for any reason, place 2 friendly Battalions on this Dropsite regardless of the number of Battalions removed or Genitor Towers on this Dropsite. If these Battalions are gained through Battalion Combat, they are placed after Battalion Combat. When this Feature is destroyed, it contributes its points to the Kill Points of the opposing player that destroyed it.

ship.lore:
The EX-7 Packet-Runner is a common courier craft used throughout the territories of the United Colonies of Mankind. Designed for routine parcel and sensitive package transport, it prioritizes simple construction and dependable operation over appearance or refinement. Most examples in service are visibly beaten up and poorly maintained, their worn hulls reflecting constant use and minimal upkeep.

They are Built around a straightforward modular frame, similar to other workhorse craft like the T-Type utility haulers and the smaller VX-22 Flesners. The EX-7 typically consists of little more than the essentials: cockpit, drive assembly, and standardized cargo racks bolted into a compact hull with the cargo containers mounted underneath.

Though rarely the focus of attention, EX-7 Packet-Runners move a constant flow of everyday freight between stations, depots, and outposts, quietly handling the unglamorous but essential task of keeping day-to-day logistics running. Colonial authorities have repurposed many of these ships for the express purpose of resupplying fighter and bomber support craft. Their cargo containers filled with factory-fresh compliments of fighters and bombers waiting for an appropriate launch platform. Experimental versions of these containers have been developed to effortlessly convert standardised hardpoints on space stations into makeshift hangar bays.

Instead of picking an Order for this Group when it activates, it may in any order; turn in any direction, move up to its Thrust, attack with any number of its weapons gaining a Spike for each additional Weapon System assigned after the first. Each option can only be chosen once per activation.
At the end of this Group's activation, if it did not gain any Spikes, remove a Spike from it.

ship.lore:
Though there has been extensive speculation on the viability or even potential existence of any kind of life adapted for the vacuum of space, none have been able to prove any hypothesis one way or another. The complete alien nature of something that could feasibly live without any kind of atmosphere or gravity pushes the limits of human speculation. Though themselves alien, every other race humanity has encountered has had a terrestrial origin. PHR expeditionary fleets have almost by accident stumbled into proof of space-based lifeforms. A solitary, anomalous creature was found in a small orange dwarf system. For an as-yet-unknown reason, this creature was traversing a veritable cosmic backwater with nought but ice and gas giants. Seemingly passive, the creature ignored the survey fleet, at least until it closed in. Initially curious, the creature allowed a single survey vessel close enough to scan, though was likely taking in all it could of the strange mechanical interloper.

It's temperament suddenly changed, however, when a second survey vessel moved to its opposite flank. Without warning, it unleashed a tentacle that damn near tore the closest ship in half. If it wasn't for the quick thinking of the crew the ship could well have been lost to the attack. The flanking ship was hit by an attack with no discernible origin. Crushing forces impacted the ship and though little structural damage was caused, they were pushed into a completely different heading and at a much reduced velocity.

Fortunately both ships had completed detailed scans of the creature, and although these are currently highly classified, news of this incredible discovery, now dubbed "The Argonaut", is reaching the ears of those back in the republic. Unfortunately, both survey ships have been prevented from returning to PHR space and have been instructed to seek the nearest safe-haven to repair and shelter. While the Solar system is hardly safe, it is the largest concentration of PHR assets within a reasonable distance, and is about as safe as anywhere else.

Fully Fuelled (2AP): At the start of a friendly Group’s activation, if that Group is within 3” and on the same Orbital Layer as a Ship with the Fuel Transporter rule, the friendly Group increases its total movement (after Orders) by 3” this round. If that Group is on the Max Thrust order, it increases its total movement (after Orders) by 6” this round instead.
If the friendly Group is C Tonnage, that Group must be within 3” and on the same Orbital Layer as two Ships with the Fuel Transporter rule instead.
Ships with the Fuel Transporter rule are unaffected by this Ability.

After completing an attack with this Weapon, this Ship is destroyed (a weapon with 0 Attack value does not roll to hit, does not cause any saves to be made, and does not inflict damage due to hits).

When this Ship is destroyed (for any reason), it explodes with a Fuel Detonation effect and a range of 3”. Ships damaged by this explosion also gain a Fire token.

ship.lore:
The Maganum Asset Bureau was once one of the largest civilian infrastructure manufacturers in the colonies prior to the inception of the UCM. Hailing from a relatively quiet colony with a focus on agriculture, the M.A.B. developed and put into service a multitude of logistical vessels. Many were designed to transport Maganum’s bountiful harvests to other colony worlds, such as the M.A.B. 45 and 46, with holds designed to keep live seafood and store masses of frozen produce, keeping the colonies main source of protein moving.

Then there was the M.A.B. 67, arguably, the Bureau’s most successful design. This transport is able to safely carry an exceptional volume of various types of fuel, from Maganum’s simple biofuels, to the hypercompressed metallic hydrogen that keeps the UCM war machine running. Built to exacting standards, the 67 has one of the strongest and most reliable power plants for a ship of its size. As it was never expected to see actual combat, the reactors do not have the automatic shutdown safeties of UCM combat ships, indeed if the ship were to see combat, it is quite possible that any damage to the reactors could cause a major containment breach, flooding compartments with highly volatile plasma.

The ubiquity of the line meant that they were scattered far and wide at the time of the Scourge invasion, now there are 67’s amongst almost all the major players of the time. The UCM have continued to produce small numbers of this ship, while M.A.B. has dwindled, they still produce original and updated designs and have mostly superseded the 67 with the much more efficient 192, a built for purpose, clearly UCM design. The Scourge have re-purposed many of these ships into water transports and rarely use them for transporting fuel, while the PHR still make use of refit variants for their logistics purposes. Many of these have been seen in resistance hands, several are part of the Vega Scrapfleet and Kalium have seemingly gotten or reverse engineered the designs to produce more ships of the class, though are much more reckless with them than any other faction.

ship.lore:
It’s a tough, thankless job hauling cargo from ground to space, but the Maganum Kinematics Mass Transporter takes it all in its stride. This reliable workhorse can be frequently seen flitting between orbit and atmosphere collecting and dispensing valuable cargo. During the reconquest, the durable, yet lightly armoured spaceframe of this vessel was used as a second line support vessel assisting troopships in setting up forward operating bases. Full of prefabricated barricades, fire-support bunkers, and even command centres, this small hauler vastly improves the efficiency of troops deployed to combat zones. Keeping the war machine well equipped, well stocked, and with a relatively comfortable, if cramped base to strike out at Scourge targets from.

Even though their primary contracts are with the UCM, Maganum Kinematics have sold many of these to other non government organisations. Various shipping magnates operate at least one of these reliable ships at each of their destinations. More surprisingly, even other factions have been making use of these vessels. The PHR stationed at Earth have requisitioned a pair of these ships, as well as Kalium counting no fewer than four of these vessels amongst its fleet, though only two have been seen operating in the vicinity of Earth.

rules.name: Gravitational Arc

On a 1-3, the Group is moved into Orbit and cannot move into Atmosphere again this round. It suffers the effects of moving through any scenery it is placed in. This takes place before that Group attacks or launches assets. If all Ships in the Group have Orbital Decay tokens, they are not affected.
This feature requires 5 or more Battalions to be removed during Battalion Combat and 5 damage to remove due to attacks.

flagship.name: Heracles Battleship
flagship.namesake: The greatest hero of Greek mythology, son of Zeus and the mortal Alcmene. Killed his own family in a divine madness sent by Hera, then spent the rest of his life earning absolution through the Twelve Labors, slaying the Nemean Lion, capturing Cerberus, diverting rivers. Worshipped across the ancient world as the patron of strength and the destroyer of monsters.

admirals.bio:
Claudia Rhee is a rarity amongst the PHR. Once a Siren, her tactical aptitude and control over countless Familiars gained her a place as a Medusa, one of the most elite members of the already elite Siren Corps. She earned her place in the captains chair when her ship was ambushed by Shaltari pirates. Their initial volley had struck right through the ship's CIC, killing many of the command crew and leaving vital systems unmanned. Acting immediately, Claudia networked her Familiars with the ships' systems, restored order and brought weapons to bear. Her quick thinking saved the lives of many that day and while the ship itself was unsalvageable, Claudia was approached with an offer that would one day see her commanding not only her own ship, but an entire fleet.

As the daughter of Octavia Rhee, there has been high expectations of her since the day she was born. Fortunately for her she has exceeded every single one of them. She was able to control multiple Familiars by the time her peers were only just able to operate a single Familiar. She aced every single combat proficiency test thrown at her and her field operation record is impeccable.

Though despite all of this she still lives in her mother's shadow, made even darker by her recent sacrifice in the Shangri-La system. While Claudia is determined to make those responsible pay, the alliances made before the Battle of Earth make this a difficult prospect as of late. It is only a matter of time, however, before that all breaks down, countless simulations calculated by her Familiars have shown her that over and over again.

admirals.name: Helena of Asgard

flagship.namesake: [Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompey) (Pompey the Great) was the Roman general who conquered the eastern Mediterranean, cleared the sea of pirates in forty days, and formed the First Triumvirate with Caesar and Crassus before civil war made them enemies. He earned the cognomen Magnus, meaning the Great, early in his career under the dictator Sulla. In Rome he dedicated the city's first permanent stone theatre, an immense complex that bore his name.

admirals.bio:
Helena of Asgard is one of the most aggressive ranking officers active in the Asgard System. Part of the force tasked with destroying as many UCM Strike Carriers as possible. Retreating groups learned to steer clear of her flagship's Heavy Quad Battery lest the entire group be obliterated.

While the UCM believe Helena is part of the external PHR forces, the truth is that Helena is an Asgard native. During the PHR's initial dealings with the resistance forces on Asgard Prime a young Helena started a rapport with PHR naval personnel, listening to tales of sights she would never see staying put on her home planet. Resolved to go with the returning PHR forces she sneaked aboard an outbound PHR transport. To her new allies, however, her infiltration attempt was painfully obvious.

Although among plenty of other Asgardians that had decided to join their PHR allies, Helena showed great enthusiasm and promise in fleet-based operations. Proving herself again and again, Helena returned to Asgard Prime shortly before the ambush on the UCM fleet.
