This Ship’s Boarding Pods and Drop Pods can only be used while it has friendly Battalions on it and each Boarding Pod or Drop Pod launched causes one friendly Battalion on this Ship to be removed.

ship.lore:
The DH-Type represents one of the Colonial Fleet's largest run of dedicated long-range prison ships, built around a standardized architecture of reinforced armour, multi-tier detention decks and automated security. Originally intended strictly for high-risk inmate transport and remote incarceration, wartime pressures pushed the class into broader operational roles.

Though designed with consistent core systems, such as compartmentalized containment blocks, automated defensive suites, ECM shielding, and a C.A.G.E emitter field. The ships grew increasingly variable due to differing missions, retrofits, and partial deactivations. Although uncommon, Individual DH-Type vessels gained their own notoriety, such as Iron Veil, Remnant Forge, Dreadhold and Bright Spire. The DH-Type ships illustrated the evolution through conversions into troop transports, logistics carriers, medical ships, and frontier support platforms, often retaining traces of their original penal infrastructure.

In modern service, L1-class hulls endure as adaptable, if austere, multi-role assets. Their durable construction, intimidating infrastructure, and legacy security systems continue to define their operational character, reflecting both the robustness of the original design and the fleet's ongoing need to repurpose coercive architecture for broader demands.

ship.lore:
The Jah'tar are an independent, if diminished, starfaring race that sails from the planet Jaheria. Over two century's peaceable trade with the UCM's colony of Platina, they have shared some of their history.

Their Time of Many Worlds ended roughly three millennia ago when the Great Adversary came. The Jah'tar do not know if any of their other planets survived. Their lifespans of roughly 35 years make this race-memory dimmer than one might expect, but parallels to mankind's own experience was clear, the Scourge were the likely culprits. Surviving artworks show cruder invading ships, but some Jah'tar technology bears limited similarity to Scourge, and most scientists believe it was absorbed and evolved by the enemy. Jah'tar ships also appear grown rather than made, although theirs are largely pseudo-organic chitin over a fine titanium weave.

The Jah'tar no longer fully understand their own technology. Possibly such knowledge was confined to their lost central worlds, but as in antiquity, all Jah'tar works radiate a passion for style and beauty. They covet precious materials and gems, driving their trade with Platina. In return, the UCM gains access to the Jaherian System's ores and wealth of rare elements essential for FTL drive core construction.

The Jah'tar are rangier than humans with stronger limbs and thick, leathery skin. Naturally placid and artistic, they move in an unhurried way but are fast when pressed. With long, prehensile tails they are agile climbers, leading to some exotic spaces aboard their ships. Their four, quad-jointed digits are equally dextrous on hands or feet, and are in constant motion, possibly as a base layer of communication. Their language is a series of rapid clicks and screeches, so they use human speech in negotiations out of respect for our limited vocal range.

Most of humanity's contact with the Jah'tar is via their famous Startraders, graceful, cruiser-sized ships with lavishly decorated meeting spaces, living areas, and cavernous holds. These vessels are permitted free passage within the Platina System but are closely monitored whenever they appear elsewhere in UCM space, despite being unarmed. Hawkish colonial admirals insist that all that internal space could be put to more nefarious uses. Some Startraders serve as mercenaries with other races in exchange for favourable trades, although the UCM occasionally utilises their services so too. Their value lies with their unique support technologies since the Jah'tar refuse to license any true warships to other's violence.

Relations with the alien Jah'tar is an aberration for the UCM, but these arrangements go back before the Scourge invasion and are frankly easier than conquest. Although Jaheria would inevitably be crushed, Jah'tar weaponry is formidable when they are forced to use it, and high casualties that humanity can ill-afford would result.

ship.lore:
M-Type Barges are the larger cousin of the L-Type. Produced at the same Tharsis Manufacturing shipyards over Mars, the M-Type was designed for corporate bulk shipping. Many and more of these were owned and operated by the enduring shipping companies of old Earth, each of them emblazoned with corporate livery. Designed and built after the L-Type, these ships feature much improved Foldspace drives as well as the latest innovations in structural bracing. Optimisations in production brought the build time on these freight behemoths down to only twice that of the L-Type.

Many of these were spared the events of the Scourge invasion, most would have been slowly moving between the colonies and the cradle worlds, far enough away to make emergency jumps to safety. The initial trade and logistics network of the UCM was built upon the backs of the M-Type, their reliability and availability gave the colonies enough trade stability to recover from the loss of the cradle worlds. M-Types are surprisingly rare in Resistance fleets, most of the captains of these ships were more interested in meeting deadlines and quotas than in doomsday predictions prior to the battle of Vega. Kalium is yet to be seen operating these ships, preferring the L-Type for combat resupply, though may potentially be using M-Types in more secure Kalium controlled systems.

Recent developments in prefabricated defensive structures have allowed a small number of these ships to carry deployable missile defence outposts in place of their normal cargo compliment. These outposts are designed to grant a foothold on a planet and supplement its missile halo while more permanent structures are built, re-purposed, or captured.

ship.lore: The Oblivion OBV64 Barge is a heavily armoured civilian vessel designed to transport extremely hazardous materials, unstable technology, failed reactors, and biohazards, too dangerous to store on planets. These ships travel discreetly between remote depots, derelict battlefields, and disposal zones. Crewed by an extensive team of highly trained specialists under strict quarantine and secrecy protocols, The Oblivion barge handles cargo that is often poorly understood or classified. Their role is to quietly remove dangerous discoveries and remnants from circulation before they can threaten the wider fleet, or attract unwanted attention.

ship.lore:
The Type-87 Terminus Harvester is a colossal reclamation vessel built to consume the unrepairable wreckage of war. Its monolithic maw engulfs chunks up to frigate tonnage, feeding them into vast crushing chambers where superheated hydraulic presses obliterate hull plating to slag. Two VX-22 Flensers detach from its hull, peeling derelicts apart and hauling scraps to their final destruction. Ancient, slow-moving, and relentless, it labours, stripping vessels down to raw material. Within its corroded halls, life is harsh. Dim corridors reek of burning metal as air filters struggle against decades of industrial smog.

The Type-87's wedge-like prow is battered and scarred, worn from decades of grinding through wreckage. Deep gouges and warped plating mark where debris crumpled beneath its relentless push, clearing the way for the behemoth behind.

A monolithic opening capable of engulfing entire frigates, feeding them into a crushing chamber spanning the volume of a megastructure. Inside, reinforced walls lined with titanic hydraulic presses grind vessels down in a superheated maelstrom of pulverized metal, reducing all to molten slag.

Equipped with two VX-22 Flensers, these small salvage vessels dock onto the Harvester's hull when idle but detach to roam wreckage fields. They Brutally peel derelicts apart piecemeal while hauling fragmented components to the crushing maw. Though technically separate, they operate as an extension of the Harvester, ensuring no usable scrap escapes consumption.

ship.name: VX-22 Flenser

specialRules.name: Payload F-1
specialRules.description:
When building your fleet, you may choose as many Payload Ships as you like— tonnage limits do not apply to these Ships, and they have no Group size. All Payload S/L Ships must be assigned to a Porter S/L Ship with the same letter. Payload Ships may not activate or be targeted until detached.
Payload Ships take up 1 of a Porter Ship’s capacity.
During the Porter Ship’s activation, if it is on an Order that allows it to Launch, you may detach one or more of its Payload Ships and place them within 3” of it. In the round they are detached, these Payloads activate together immediately as part of the Porter Ship’s activation after it has completed its Order. In subsequent rounds, all your Payload Ships count as being part of a single Group. Crippling Effects, Spikes, and other rules that affect an entire Group only affect the targeted Payload Ship.
Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.
If a Payload Ship is attached to a Porter Ship when that Ship is destroyed, the Payload Ship is destroyed.

A Ship with this rule can have a maximum of 3 scrap tokens at any one time. Whenever another Ship within 6" of a friendly Ship with this rule is destroyed, pick one of those friendly Ships, that Ship gains a scrap token.

ship.lore:
The VX-22 Flensers are compact salvage vessels designed for brutal ship dismantling. Their prow mounted sawblades don't cut cleanly, they tear, shred, and rip through wreckage with unrestrained violence. Designed for aggressive reclamation, they are the smaller, more aggressive sibling to the T-Type Tugboat. Where the Tugboat manoeuvres and stabilizes wreckage for controlled processing, the Flensers gut derelicts with reckless brutality, prioritizing destruction over precision.

Heavy rotating saws brutally cut through hull plating, breaking it into manageable pieces and scattering debris as they progress. Instead of delicate incision, the Flensers' sawblades operate at maximum torque, chewing through reinforced bulkheads with enough force to buckle surrounding structure.

Their cutting mechanisms frequently overheat, causing violent energy surges that make their hulls shudder mid operation.

The Flenser hurls debris into the Type-87 Terminus Harvester's compactor bay, sometimes suffering brutal kickback as the churning machinery spits chunks back out. When it happens, the debris slams into its failing frame, worsening the damage and making every load a gamble.

Positioned below the cockpit, this reinforced plating shields pilots from wreckage kicked up during cutting operations. Sloped for maximum deflection, it redirects debris that could slam into the hull with deadly force, absorbing impacts before they buckle metal or breach compartments.

ship.name: PRK-91 Provenance Ark

Mutant Fauna tokens are not Battalions and cannot control or contest a Dropsite. When any player deploys any number of Battalions to that Dropsite, if that Dropsite has any Mutant Fauna tokens, those Battalions are only placed on a roll of a 5+. If any Battalions are not placed this way, remove a Mutant Fauna token from that Dropsite. If a Dropsite starts a round with a Mutant Fauna token, remove that token at the end of the round.

specialRules.name: Expansive Radiator Systems

This ship's Fighters & Bombers use the stats of its parent fleet (if you included this ship in a Scourge fleet, its Fighters & Bombers would follow the Scourge Fighters & Bombers rules).

ship.lore:
A monolithic vessel of unimaginable scale, the Provenance Ark dwarfs most ships. A precursor to the modular construction found on Coloniser class vessels, these ships were a talisman of hope and expansionism. These are the first major terraforming vessels built by mankind, reaching out into an unknown universe. Built to prepare entire worlds for habitation, it carries vast stores of genetic material, atmospheric stabilizers, and autonomous resource systems. The Ark monitors planetary progress through an extensive network of sensors and automated regulators, adjusting atmospheric composition, maintaining microbial balance, and even modulating gravitational and magnetic fields to stabilize emerging terrains.

Entire cities once mere schematics, rise, with power grids, transport arteries, and habitation modules ready long before the first settlers arrive. Inside, Construction drones and biotic cultivators orchestrate the birth of forests, oceans, and breathable atmospheres with the precision of a master artisan.

Many ships of this class feature underslung terraforming torpedo launchers. While near useless in ship to ship combat, these torpedoes are geared towards atmospheric re-entry and contain a plethora of mutagens and nerve agents, some of which would be used on Senator class battlecruisers. Under normal circumstances the use of these would constitute a war crime. Here they are simply used to rid prospective landing areas of their megafauna, causing mass hysteria and aggression in local fauna. Any issues with unruly creatures take care of themselves, and those left over can be cut down by specialised anti-fauna vehicles. Once the LZ is cleared of hostiles, the terraformer can then deploy more traditional terraforming methods.

ship.name: Avram Bei - Subatomic Heavy Destroyer

specialRules.name: Hero
specialRules.description: You can only include two Groups with this special rule in your fleet. You cannot assign an Admiral to this Ship when building your fleet.

specialRules.name: Unique

ship.lore:
Neutron missiles are a rightly feared branch of PHR weapons technology, but until now they have been confined to the largest capital ships due to warhead core containment requirements prior to launch. A single new ship, Subatomic, has a full battery of these top-tier munitions though, complimented with twinned lasers, despite its slightly enlarged destroyer tonnage. It’s understood that this ship has yet to receive clearance for wider construction. Possible crew losses due to containment failures have been rumoured although secrecy surrounds the vessel.

Its famous captain, Avram Bei, is part of a splinter fleet that has yet to declare for one side or the other in the PHR’s recent schism, preferring to focus on their bloody pursuit of Shaltari pirates near Aaru before considering theological matters, or whether theology is even the right way of thinking about the White Sphere. Bei is a practical, non-nonsense warrior with little interest in the big picture. He is known to relish fighting at the heart of any engagement, a joy undimmed even though half of his frequently injured body has been replaced with combat augmetics.

ship.name: Camilla Felix - Nanomatrix Heavy Cruiser

specialRules.name: Hero
specialRules.description: You can only include two Groups with this special rule in your fleet. You cannot assign an Admiral to this Ship when building your fleet.

specialRules.name: Regenerate-3
specialRules.description: This Ship recovers 3 lost Hull Points at the end of its activation.

specialRules.name: Unique

specialRules.name: Repair Nanomachines
specialRules.description: Friendly Ships within 6” of this Ship that roll to repair Crippling Effects during the Repair step of the End Phase improve the results of those rolls by 2. Other friendly Ships that end their activation within 6” of this Ship on the same Orbital Layer recover 2 lost Hull Points.

ship.lore:
Camilla Felix is the younger sister of renowned war leader and, to some, heretic, Aurellia Felix. Just as charismatic but more hot-headed, which limited her advancement in a Grand Fleet naval career, Camilla is known for her individualism, humanity, and skill in war. When Aurellia declared her intention to schism along with her forces, Camilla was among a flotilla of ardent followers of the White Sphere. Given her sister’s actions, an arrest was apparently attempted, but Camilla’s crew stood with her, repelled the boarders, and helped her masterfully shoot her way out of newly hostile space in the first widely documented PHR-on-PHR combat.

She brought with her the Nanomatrix, an apparently unique vessel of heavy cruiser tonnage. A more advanced design than regular classes, this ship features an additional primary engine, a sleeker hull, and a prow-mounted energy glaive supported by a state-of-the-art power core. The vessel’s main feature however is a grossly oversized nanomachine hive, enabling both repair and offensive actions with storms of ultra-advanced nanomachines. The presumably huge cost of all this may have limited this class to one example, budget must trouble the Grand Fleet as it does the UCMF.

ship.name: EX-7 Packet Runner

specialRules.name: Monitor
specialRules.description: Ships with this rule may not use Course Change or Max Thrust orders.

specialRules.name: Reinforced Armour

specialRules.name: Feature Carrier
specialRules.description: This ship starts the game carrying a single deployable Hangar Feature (see 7.4.2 Deploying Features and 11.3 Features).

specialRules.name: Space Trucker
specialRules.description: This Ship's Hangar Deployable Feature can only be deployed to Space Stations (of any type).

specialRules.name: Mercenary
specialRules.description: This Ship may be used in any Fleet regardless of faction. When taken as part of your fleet, this Ship loses its Boardable and Civilian Transport rules.

ship.lore:
The EX-7 Packet-Runner is a common courier craft used throughout the territories of the United Colonies of Mankind. Designed for routine parcel and sensitive package transport, it prioritizes simple construction and dependable operation over appearance or refinement. Most examples in service are visibly beaten up and poorly maintained, their worn hulls reflecting constant use and minimal upkeep.

They are Built around a straightforward modular frame, similar to other workhorse craft like the T-Type utility haulers and the smaller VX-22 Flesners. The EX-7 typically consists of little more than the essentials: cockpit, drive assembly, and standardized cargo racks bolted into a compact hull with the cargo containers mounted underneath.

Though rarely the focus of attention, EX-7 Packet-Runners move a constant flow of everyday freight between stations, depots, and outposts, quietly handling the unglamorous but essential task of keeping day-to-day logistics running. Colonial authorities have repurposed many of these ships for the express purpose of resupplying fighter and bomber support craft. Their cargo containers filled with factory-fresh compliments of fighters and bombers waiting for an appropriate launch platform. Experimental versions of these containers have been developed to effortlessly convert standardised hardpoints on space stations into makeshift hangar bays.

ship.name: Argonaut

specialRules.name: Impetuous
specialRules.description: At the start of each round, friendly Groups with this rule improve the Lock of their Weapon Systems by 1 until you activate a friendly Group without this rule.

specialRules.description:
This weapon can only be used against targets in base contact.
When you inflict damage with this weapon, you may remove a Spike from this Group, if you do, the defending Group gains a Spike.

specialRules.name: Mind of its Own
specialRules.description:
This Ship can be used in any fleet, regardless of faction but does not count towards point spent on M Tonnage Ships when building your fleet. This Ship cannot have an Admiral assigned to it for any reason.
Instead of picking an Order for this Group when it activates, it may in any order; turn in any direction, move up to its Thrust, attack with any number of its weapons gaining a Spike for each additional Weapon System assigned after the first. Each option can only be chosen once per activation.
At the end of this Group's activation, if it did not gain any Spikes, remove a Spike from it.

ship.lore:
Though there has been extensive speculation on the viability or even potential existence of any kind of life adapted for the vacuum of space, none have been able to prove any hypothesis one way or another. The complete alien nature of something that could feasibly live without any kind of atmosphere or gravity pushes the limits of human speculation. Though themselves alien, every other race humanity has encountered has had a terrestrial origin. PHR expeditionary fleets have almost by accident stumbled into proof of space-based lifeforms. A solitary, anomalous creature was found in a small orange dwarf system. For an as-yet-unknown reason, this creature was traversing a veritable cosmic backwater with nought but ice and gas giants. Seemingly passive, the creature ignored the survey fleet, at least until it closed in. Initially curious, the creature allowed a single survey vessel close enough to scan, though was likely taking in all it could of the strange mechanical interloper.

It's temperament suddenly changed, however, when a second survey vessel moved to its opposite flank. Without warning, it unleashed a tentacle that damn near tore the closest ship in half. If it wasn't for the quick thinking of the crew the ship could well have been lost to the attack. The flanking ship was hit by an attack with no discernible origin. Crushing forces impacted the ship and though little structural damage was caused, they were pushed into a completely different heading and at a much reduced velocity.

Fortunately both ships had completed detailed scans of the creature, and although these are currently highly classified, news of this incredible discovery, now dubbed "The Argonaut", is reaching the ears of those back in the republic. Unfortunately, both survey ships have been prevented from returning to PHR space and have been instructed to seek the nearest safe-haven to repair and shelter. While the Solar system is hardly safe, it is the largest concentration of PHR assets within a reasonable distance, and is about as safe as anywhere else.

ship.name: M.A.B. 67 Fuel Transport

specialRules.description: This Ship may make an additional turn at any point during its movement, regardless of the Order its Group has taken.

specialRules.name: Fuel Transporter
specialRules.description:
While a Ship with this rule is on the table, you have access to the following Ability:

Fully Fuelled (2AP): At the start of a friendly Group’s activation, if that Group is within 3” and on the same Orbital Layer as a Ship with the Fuel Transporter rule, the friendly Group increases its total movement (after Orders) by 3” this round. If that Group is on the Max Thrust order, it increases its total movement (after Orders) by 6” this round instead.
If the friendly Group is C Tonnage, that Group must be within 3” and on the same Orbital Layer as two Ships with the Fuel Transporter rule instead.
Ships with the Fuel Transporter rule are unaffected by this Ability.

specialRules.name: Ignite Reserves
specialRules.description:
After completing an attack with this Weapon, this Ship is destroyed (a weapon with 0 Attack value does not roll to hit, does not cause any saves to be made, and does not inflict damage due to hits).

When this Ship is destroyed (for any reason), it explodes with a Fuel Detonation effect and a range of 3”. Ships damaged by this explosion also gain a Fire token.

specialRules.name: Mercenary
specialRules.description: This Ship may be used in any Fleet regardless of faction. When taken as part of your fleet, this Ship loses its Boardable and Civilian Transport rules.

ship.lore:
The Maganum Asset Bureau was once one of the largest civilian infrastructure manufacturers in the colonies prior to the inception of the UCM. Hailing from a relatively quiet colony with a focus on agriculture, the M.A.B. developed and put into service a multitude of logistical vessels. Many were designed to transport Maganum’s bountiful harvests to other colony worlds, such as the M.A.B. 45 and 46, with holds designed to keep live seafood and store masses of frozen produce, keeping the colonies main source of protein moving.

Then there was the M.A.B. 67, arguably, the Bureau’s most successful design. This transport is able to safely carry an exceptional volume of various types of fuel, from Maganum’s simple biofuels, to the hypercompressed metallic hydrogen that keeps the UCM war machine running. Built to exacting standards, the 67 has one of the strongest and most reliable power plants for a ship of its size. As it was never expected to see actual combat, the reactors do not have the automatic shutdown safeties of UCM combat ships, indeed if the ship were to see combat, it is quite possible that any damage to the reactors could cause a major containment breach, flooding compartments with highly volatile plasma.

The ubiquity of the line meant that they were scattered far and wide at the time of the Scourge invasion, now there are 67’s amongst almost all the major players of the time. The UCM have continued to produce small numbers of this ship, while M.A.B. has dwindled, they still produce original and updated designs and have mostly superseded the 67 with the much more efficient 192, a built for purpose, clearly UCM design. The Scourge have re-purposed many of these ships into water transports and rarely use them for transporting fuel, while the PHR still make use of refit variants for their logistics purposes. Many of these have been seen in resistance hands, several are part of the Vega Scrapfleet and Kalium have seemingly gotten or reverse engineered the designs to produce more ships of the class, though are much more reckless with them than any other faction.

ship.name: MK Mass Transporter

specialRules.name: Descent

When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.
When attacking into Orbit from Atmosphere, any attack always hits on a 6+.
A non-Descent Ship that ends its activation in Atmosphere takes D3 damage. Colossal Ships take 2D3 damage instead.

Battalion Support (1AP): Once per activation, when you deploy Battalions from a Group on any Orbital Layer within 6” of a friendly Ship with the Bulk Lighter rule, choose one of the launching Asset types. If the chosen Asset is either Dropships or Drop Pods, place an additional Battalion. If the chosen Asset is Bulk Landers, place an additional two Battalions. Other Launch Assets are unaffected by this Ability.

ship.lore:
It’s a tough, thankless job hauling cargo from ground to space, but the Maganum Kinematics Mass Transporter takes it all in its stride. This reliable workhorse can be frequently seen flitting between orbit and atmosphere collecting and dispensing valuable cargo. During the reconquest, the durable, yet lightly armoured spaceframe of this vessel was used as a second line support vessel assisting troopships in setting up forward operating bases. Full of prefabricated barricades, fire-support bunkers, and even command centres, this small hauler vastly improves the efficiency of troops deployed to combat zones. Keeping the war machine well equipped, well stocked, and with a relatively comfortable, if cramped base to strike out at Scourge targets from.

Even though their primary contracts are with the UCM, Maganum Kinematics have sold many of these to other non government organisations. Various shipping magnates operate at least one of these reliable ships at each of their destinations. More surprisingly, even other factions have been making use of these vessels. The PHR stationed at Earth have requisitioned a pair of these ships, as well as Kalium counting no fewer than four of these vessels amongst its fleet, though only two have been seen operating in the vicinity of Earth.

flagship.namesake: [Mount Olympus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Olympus) is the highest mountain in Greece and, in Greek myth, the home of the twelve Olympian gods. Its cloud-wreathed peak was held to be the seat of Zeus and the council of the gods.

admirals.bio:
Originally conscripted from one of the poorest locales on Kalium, Nguen has seen a meteoric rise through the ranks of the Kalium navy. He has proven himself time and time again for the Kabal, his first command would see him trade blows with the Shaltari in anti-piracy actions protecting valuable in-system shipping routes.

Since his start as a Vent Cannon technician, Nguen has gained an intimate understanding of the technology and physics behind the devastating weapons. Preferring commands on ships equipped with the unstable weapons, he's reduced scores of ships to molten metal, very few of which were his own.

The defining point of his career was the destruction of a trio of scourge battlecruisers with his previous command, a Gladiator class Grand Cruiser. Suffering serious damage after the destruction of one and the crippling of another, a final volley of vent fire overloaded the ships reactor. Ordering the ship to fly at full thrust towards the third and the call to abandon ship, Nguen would soon watch the reactor consume both his ship and the enemy battlecruiser from the relative safety of his escape vessel.

Upon his return to Kalium, Nguen and his surviving crew would be assigned to the nearly complete Grosses Messer, overseeing its final reactor adjustments and being tasked with a live fire shakedown cruise.

admirals.name: Hagen

abilities.name: Reinforce Systems
abilities.effect: When a friendly Ship of H or C tonnage would roll its Backup save due to an attack, improve its Backup save for that attack by 1.

flagship.name: Tribune Battlecruiser

specialRules.description: Groups with this rule may begin the game Directly Deployed, ignoring the normal Scenario Deployment and Approach Types (though still counting towards Groups Directly Deployed). If it does, it may be deployed up to 3” away from your Deployment Zone.

flagship.namesake: A tribune, a senior Roman officer of the legions, or the people's elected champion against the power of the Senate.

admirals.bio:
The Flagship of the independent High Technician known as Hagen is believed to have once belonged to the Kalium Kabal. Though quite why they would relinquish a working Battlecruiser to independents is currently unknown to UCM intelligence. Any chance to communicate and question those in Hagen's fleet state that it was "empty when we found it" and that the ship is "legitimate salvage".

Regardless of how these independents acquired this ship, they seem more than capable of using and maintaining it. Having taken part in the battles above Luna, the Fortune's Fancy scored Hagen and his fleet several Scourge kills. The Fortune's Fancy is suspected to be highly modified, capable of carrying its standard launch compliment, along with a pair of internally stored torpedoes. Observations by the UCMF Saccharine show that these torpedoes are launched in the crudest way possible. Simply being allowed to float outwards from the bulk lander bays and fired while free floating.

admirals.name: Typhoon Vasquez

admirals.bio:
Typhoon Vasquez is the Head Engineer of the Red Baron, a pre-war ship used as a test-bed for various ammunition types designed for then-current Artillery Cannons. Vasquez's Battlegroup contains a large number of industrial ships, including the Andar Errente, a pre-war Industrial Raft. Thanks to copious amounts of manufacturing ability, Vasquez is able to be very liberal with the application of the various bootleg munitions produced by his fleet.

Vasquez's combat capable ships were present at the Battle for Earth and managed to score several Scourge kills. The Red Baron spent most of the engagement firing on any and every cylinder it could find. Vasquez's battle tactics seemed to either be genius, drawing most of the Scourge return fire towards the Red Baron and its ablative armour, or the absolute lunacy of being on constant weapons-free.

ship.name: Coloniser Interstellar Dreadnought

specialRules.name: Command Ship-2
specialRules.description: Increase the Level of any Admiral assigned to this Ship by 2.

ship.lore: A noteworthy Coloniser was the Supernova - colloquially known as the “HMS S**tstorm”. During the battle of Vega-4 this derelict colonyship was lashed with as many Heavy Vent Cannons as the hull could support and crewed by a skeleton crew of heroes who knew they were not coming back.  The Supernova then drifted into the mass of the enemy fleet and unleashed superheated plasma until there was almost nothing left of either fleet.
ship.rulesText: This Ship must take a total of eight options from the Dreadnought Systems list. Up to four options may be taken from the Broadside Hardpoint category. Up to four options may be taken from the Turrets category. Up to four options may be taken from the Launch Hardpoint category. Up to two options may be taken from the Structures category.

ship.name: Explorer Interstellar Ark

specialRules.name: Command Ship-1
specialRules.description: Increase the Level of any Admiral assigned to this Ship by 1.

ship.lore: Explorers are battleship-sized beasts, built from more standard modules than Pathfinders. Larger exploration fleets would typically be headed by one. Although most would morph over their storied lives, each was once famous among Earth’s populace. Supremely tough, adaptable and repairable, each is valued by Resistance admirals, who usually max-out the platform’s armament. Rarely, they survive in their original configuration - finding the lonely, becalmed Edensphere was a revelation to the UCM - a self-sustaining Amazon ecosystem, she is a final testament to Earth’s lost biodiversity. Most Explorers are brutal chop-shop jobs of multiple ships with working modules swapped in for expediency. In their first day’s fighting during the Battle for Earth, the Vega Scrapfleet famously jumped the crippled Santa Maria back to their staging area and had her back in action within 48 hours, looking quite different. The grandest of these dinosaurs are known as Colonisers - among the largest ships ever built by mankind, they exceed modern dreadnoughts in displacement. Once they carried whole populations toward their new lives, now they end them en-mass.
ship.rulesText: This Ship must take a total of six options from the Dreadnought Systems list. Up to three options may be taken from the Broadside Hardpoint category. Up to three options may be taken from the Turrets category. Up to three options may be taken from the Launch Hardpoint category. A single option may be taken from the Structures category.

ship.name: Pathfinder Interstellar Raft
ship.lore: Among mankind’s oldest FTL-capable ships, Pathfinders offer resistance admirals extreme toughness and flexibility in a battlecruiser-sized package. These mighty vessels once boldly plied new space, often commanding smaller exploration fleets on random jump expeditions. Missions lasting years made bulk essential, since aid or resupply was never assured, given the rarity of FTL-capable ships in those heady days. Once humanity broke from their unequal alliance with the Shaltari, alien raids were a frequent problem. Central to the design brief was reparability in the field and mission-specific configuration. Unlike most ships, whole sections of superstructure can be swapped out for specialist modules, including weapons, storage, hangars, refineries, factories, cores and even vast bio-domes to seed empty planets with Earth’s fauna and flora. Since every expedition was unique, no two Pathfinders are identical. Today, these ancient vessels perfectly suit the Resistance and are frequently armed beyond their historic configurations. Like most pre-war designs, Kalium still builds Pathfinders, although why they have built quite so many of these fighting exploration ships vexes the UCM’s High Council.
ship.rulesText: This Ship must take a total of four options from the Dreadnought Systems list. Up to two options may be taken from the Broadside Hardpoint category. Up to two options may be taken from the Turrets category. Up to two options may be taken from the Launch Hardpoint category. A single option may be taken from the Structures category.

ship.name: Yamamoto Grand Battleship
ship.lore: The Yamamoto is a class of grand battleship designed and constructed by the EAA prior to the arrival of the Scourge. Designed alongside the Nimitz-class, the Yamamoto is one of the last grand battleships built by twinning the hulls of existing battleships. Unlike its sister class, it took an alternate approach to enabling the spinal vent lance, forgoing launch bays in favour of an even more enlarged power core. This allowed the Yamamoto to mount a pair of 9K mass driver turrets as secondary weapons, making it even more deadly when going weapons-free. To fill out the remainder of its power budget, a pair of chin-mounted torpedo launchers were added, giving the class even more ship-killing power. By virtue of its loadout, the Yamamoto proved an exceptional threat against individually tough targets, though its primary weapon's instability means its captain must carefully judge between maximising damage or potentially broiling the engineering team assigned to maintain it.
ship.rulesText: This Ship may take an Engine Refit for +45 points, increasing its Thrust by 2”.
ship.namesake: [Isoroku Yamamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isoroku_Yamamoto) (1884-1943), the Japanese admiral who conceived and directed the attack on Pearl Harbor. He studied at Harvard University and served two postings in the United States, leaving him wary of provoking a war he believed Japan could not ultimately win. An early champion of naval aviation, he steered the Imperial Japanese Navy away from battleships toward aircraft carriers. He was killed in 1943 when American fighters intercepted his aircraft over the Solomon Islands.

ship.name: Nimitz Grand Battleship
ship.lore: The Nimitz is a class of grand battleship designed and constructed in the pre-Scourge era, and is one of the last classes built by twinning existing battleship hulls (alongside its sister class, the Yamamoto). While the shipbuilding technique was crude, it offered more flexibility in its modularity versus the newer, purpose-built grand battleship classes. As a result, the class proved the perfect test bed for the spinal vent lance, a risky experiment made cost-viable by its construction method. The vent lance proved to be the largest vent cannon ever built, necessitating a massive hull and extremely high power requirements. Owing to this power draw, the Nimitz mounts NC-16 missile turrets as secondary weapons alongside hangar bays. Despite the extreme hazards of carrying such a large vent cannon, several Nimitz battleships have survived into the modern day, where they are fielded by Resistance fleets, including Kalium, their superlative ship-killing power well worth the trade-off of occasionally cooking entire engineering teams.

ship.namesake: Fleet Admiral [Chester Nimitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_W._Nimitz) (1885-1966), commander of US naval forces across the Pacific in the Second World War. He began his career as a submariner and helped pioneer the U.S. Navy's early diesel submarine force. He was promoted to the five-star rank of Fleet Admiral in December 1944 and signed the Japanese surrender for the United States aboard the USS Missouri. The supercarrier USS Nimitz was later named in his honour.

ship.name: Drake Grand Battleship

weapons.name: Spinal Mass Annihilator
weapons.special: Bloom-1, Crippling, Critical-2, Focused, High Power

ship.lore: The Drake class was the first human vessel to mount an apocalypse-grade, non-nuclear weapon: the Spinal Mass Annihilator. It is an enormous kinetic energy weapon capable of driving a house-sized lump of tungsten carbide coated, ultra-dense metal clean through a battleship, lengthwise. Such a weapon required enlarged power cores aboard the twinned Old Battleships and the new central core to feed it, necessitating the loss of its broadsides. Secondary armaments include NC-16 missile turrets and a pair of heavy vent canons to burst surplus energy onto any survivors.
ship.rulesText: This Ship may take an Engine Refit for +45 points, increasing its Thrust by 2”. Spinal Mass Annihilator If damage from this weapon or any Crippling Effect it would cause would destroy a ship, remove that ship from the game without rolling for Explosion.
ship.namesake: [Sir Francis Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Drake) (c.1540-1596), the English privateer and explorer, second to circumnavigate the globe and scourge of Spain. He served as vice admiral of the English fleet that repelled the Spanish Armada in 1588, commanding the galleon Revenge. He was elected Mayor of Plymouth and twice sat in Parliament.

ship.name: Farragut Grand Battleship
ship.lore: Developed alongside the Barbarossa, the Farragut offers a more straightforward weapons loadout with surplus power capacity. This surplus and the relative simplicity of its armaments gave the Farragut legendary endurance and has made it a favourite of Resistance fleets. Offering the same quad-turret NC-16 battery and NC-12 broadsides as the Barbarossa, the Farragut also mounts six enormous torpedoes in three tubes, allowing for two devastating spreads. Few ships can survive a single salvo from this ancient leviathan.
ship.rulesText: This Ship may take an Engine Refit for +45 points, increasing its Thrust by 2”.
ship.namesake: [David Farragut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Farragut) (1801-1870), the first admiral of the US Navy, remembered for 'Damn the torpedoes, full speed ahead.'. He entered the navy as a midshipman at the age of nine and captured New Orleans for the Union in 1862. Congress created the ranks of rear admiral and later full admiral expressly to honour his service.

variants.namesake: Myrmidon was, in Greek myth, the eponymous ancestor of the Myrmidons, the fiercely disciplined warriors who followed Achilles to Troy.

ship.lore: A specialist variant of the Nelson, the Barbarossa replaces the power-hungry, early mass driver turrets with NC-16 missiles. In addition to offering increased lethality at close range, this frees up power for an enormous scanner array. Unlike most vessels with a detector role, the Barbarossa typically fights at the forefront of any engagement, caring little for the increased visibility that comes with running active scanners due to its already vast signature. To fully utilise the remaining power, the class’s lethality was further bolstered by a pair of chin-mounted vent canons.
ship.rulesText: This Ship may take an Engine Refit for +45 points, increasing its Thrust by 2”. When this Ship uses its Detector special rule, you may place an additional two Spikes on a different enemy Group in line of sight.
ship.namesake: [Hayreddin Barbarossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayreddin_Barbarossa) (c.1478-1546), the corsair who became grand admiral of the Ottoman fleet and ruled the Mediterranean. Born on the island of Lesbos, he inherited the name Barbarossa from his elder brother Oruc. His decisive victory at the Battle of Preveza in 1538 secured Ottoman naval dominance over the Mediterranean for decades.

ship.name: Yi Sun-sin Grand Battleship
ship.lore: The Kabal’s readiness to trade losses for victory perfectly matches the unstable savagery of this colossus.
ship.rulesText: This Ship may take an Engine Refit for +45 points, increasing its Thrust by 2”.
ship.namesake: [Yi Sun-sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yi_Sun-sin) (1545-1598), the Korean admiral whose armoured 'turtle ships' crushed far larger Japanese fleets without a single defeat. At the Battle of Myeongnyang in 1597 he is said to have routed a vastly larger Japanese fleet with only a handful of ships. He was killed by a stray bullet at the Battle of Noryang in 1598 and ordered his death kept secret so the fight could go on.

ship.name: Nelson Grand Battleship
ship.lore: The Nelson is a class of grand battleship constructed during the pre-Scourge era, and stands as one of the first grand battleship classes built by humanity. After humanity's relationship with the Shaltari soured, the EAA found itself woefully outgunned by the suddenly-hostile alien race. Rather than commit to a costly scrapping process, shipbuilders hastily twinned existing battleship hulls around newer, vastly-improved power cores. These new ships, dubbed "grand battleships", featured significantly improved scanners, armaments and point defences while offering better survivability. One of the first built this way, the Nelson was created by pairing two Musashi battleships together. The reliability of the overbuilt Musashi hull, coupled with its low-power-draw weapons, made the Nelson a potent and survivable threat against the Shaltari forces of the era. Many have survived to the modern day, employed by independent Resistance crews and Kalium alike.
ship.rulesText: This Ship may take an Engine Refit for +45 points, increasing its Thrust by 2”.
ship.namesake: [Admiral Horatio Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Nelson,_1st_Viscount_Nelson) (1758-1805), who shattered the Franco-Spanish fleet at Trafalgar and died in the hour of victory. He lost the sight in his right eye at Corsica and his right arm at Tenerife. His destruction of the French fleet at the Battle of the Nile in 1798 stranded Napoleon's army in Egypt.

ship.name: Vanguard Old Battleship
ship.lore: EAAS Vanguard was once the only example of her class. A development of the earlier Iowa, she incorporated vent canon broadsides and what was once a state-of-the-art power core. She proved unstable due to her armament and insufficient cooling and was ultimately lost with all hands over Eden Prime during the Scourge invasion. However, her plans were widely available due to her age, and since then, many foolhardy and/or bloodthirsty resistance admirals have converted Musashis and Lexingtons into Vanguards using more recent cores and custom-built vent canons.
ship.namesake: [HMS Vanguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Vanguard_(1944)), the last and largest battleship ever built for the Royal Navy, completed just after the Second World War.

ship.name: Iowa Old Battleship
ship.lore: Much rarer than its sister classes, the Iowa was the earliest known testbed of vent cannon technology. It mounts a pair of turreted heavy vent canons by dispensing with any broadside armament, freeing up space for a much enlarged, antique power core. Ventral NC-16 missiles complete the Iowa’s armament, given their negligible power drain. Like all Old Battleships, the Iowa has poor scanners and point defences by modern standards, necessitating careful use.
ship.namesake: [USS Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Iowa_(BB-61)) (BB-61), lead ship of the US Navy's last class of battleships, famed for her nine 16-inch guns.

ship.name: Lexington Old Battleship
ship.lore: Like other Old Battleships, the Lexington could rightly belong in a museum, although it’s still a formidable warship today. Many survived the Scourge invasion since they were mostly relegated to frontier picket duty, being outmoded even then. In the hard centuries that followed, the Lexington has proven its worth countless times, offering a reliable loadout of NC-16 missiles, a single ventral torpedo, and a fair-sized strike craft hangar. The negligible power drain of all of these gives the class excellent toughness, endurance, and utility for its age.
ship.namesake: [USS Lexington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Lexington_(CV-2)), the US aircraft carrier nicknamed 'Lady Lex', lost in the Battle of the Coral Sea in 1942.

ship.name: Musashi Old Battleship
ship.lore: Once among the mightiest ships ever built by mankind, the Musashi is now a relic, even among resistance fleets. Introduced in the mid-24th century, around the time of first contact with the Shaltari, the youngest of these veterans is over 300 years old. However, they were overbuilt for the rigours of exploration and have proven supremely reliable. Its broadsides of chemically fired N-12 cannons are undemanding workhorses with a low power draw, so most Musashi’s spinal turrets have been refitted with 9K mass drivers over the centuries.
ship.namesake: The Japanese battleship [Musashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi), among the two largest ever built, sunk under a hail of US air attacks in 1944.

ship.lore: The Tribune is heavier, slower and tougher than modern battlecruisers. It shares a superstructure and one mass driver turret with the more common Phalanx class. The remainder of its firepower comes from two conventional cannon turrets and an increased close action capability. However, the Tribune is unusual for a full combat ship of this size in that it features capacity for bulk landers. Its only real modern descendants are the PHR’s assault troopships. In addition though, the Tribune has a significant flight deck, making it a fleet carrier as well. In combination, the Tribune is a jack of all trades, able to adapt to fluid combat situations better than most ships.
ship.namesake: A [tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribune), a senior Roman officer of the legions, or the people's elected champion against the power of the Senate.

ship.lore: Sharing many superstructure elements with the smaller Centurion Grand Cruiser, the Phalanx was one of the largest standardised classes produced by Trident Industrial, though today it's only built in Kalium's yards. Pre-war Battlecruisers differ from modern types in that they are slower and offer less firepower in manoeuvre, but far superior toughness. Indeed, it's best to think of them as pocket- battleships rather than specialist, aggressive ships. The Phalanx is armed with long broadsides of transition mass drivers and four Titanmetall 9K mass drivers in two traversable turrets. In combination, the class can unleash withering fire against multiple targets, given the right positioning.
ship.namesake: The [phalanx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phalanx), the dense wall of spears and shields with which Greek and Macedonian armies broke their foes.

ship.lore: The Triumvir has been one of the most valued ships to the Resistance since escaping the Scourge invasion. Shipyards mostly being a lost luxury, any repairs had to be run in the void with the help of other ships - the Triumvir’s specialty. Though a military vessel with fighting armour and battlecruiser tonnage, most of its superstructure is dominated by an insectile bank of extending service armatures. Long-term, Triumvirs can run complex repairs that take weeks. In battle they inject expanding, rapid-cure polymer foam into hull breaches, armour cracks and voided areas, keeping a ship in the fight longer. Despite their value beyond the battlespace, many Resistance admirals gladly risk fielding Triumvirs for the sake of the greater good. To support its activities, the Triumvir has a large internal hangar for various service craft from shuttles to engineering barges. Triumvirs that go to battle tend to replace some of these with regular fighters and bombers to add offensive and escort capability.
ship.namesake: A [triumvir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triumvirate), one of the three men who shared supreme power in Rome's triumvirates, such as Caesar, Pompey and Crassus.

ship.lore: The Senator was classified at the time of the Scourge invasion and for good reason. The class was an affront to many EAA government cornerstones. Though records were lost in the invasion, historians believe the Senator was secretly developed by Earth Fleet Command’s shadowy Section Green, without civilian government knowledge. If true the military was preparing contingencies for city-wide insurrections; if not the government was. Some whisper that a military coup was tabled and this was an anti-uprising deterrent, though the Scourge put paid to anyone’s plans. Though comparatively rare then, most Senators survived the invasion since friendly fire on a biblical scale would have resulted if such terrors were used in “defence”. Kalium is rumoured to build these new - disquieting, if unsurprising. The Senator carries three armoured VX nerve agent torpedoes packed with dispersal cluster bomblets. If detonated over a city, any contact with the agent results in spasms, vomiting, paralysis and asphyxiation, leaving infrastructure untouched. As a terror weapon, the Senator carries no significant long range anti-ship firepower, but does include powerful missile turrets for close defence. Combat doctrine stressed the use of the Senator’s then advanced detector array to  warn of enemy vessels, or roving reporters after the scandal of the century.

variants.name: Vicarius
variants.lore:
While the Senator class battlecruiser was an abhorrent and unsanctioned creation of certain paranoid admirals, EAAS Vicarius was downright infamous. She was once the sole example of her class and, it is now understood, instrumental in the Cleansing of Wolfrum. In 2495, twelve years before the Scourge invasion, the mining colony of Wolfrum rebelled, violently. Soon, an unknown vessel of battlecruiser tonnage appeared above the capital and unleashed a spread of VX gas bombardment munitions, slaughtering the entire population.

No comment was made by the military and the government vehemently denied involvement. Senior individuals were executed in the following years, and often for crimes that should have warranted prison sentences. EAAS Vicarius next appeared as a loner in 2674, her decks cold with a sparse skeleton crew. Her senior officers had apparently boarded another human vessel and had not returned. Now, in 2679, new examples of her class have been spotted among Kalium’s sinister vanguard fleets.
variants.namesake: Vicarius is Latin for 'substitute' or 'deputy', one who acts with another's authority in their place. It is the root of the English word 'vicar'.

ship.namesake: A [senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Senate), one of the elder statesmen of the Roman Senate, the council that steered the Republic and Empire.

ship.name: Gladiator Grand Cruiser
ship.lore: The Gladiator was a limited production test-bed for Vent Cannon technology, developed from the Centurion class by Equatorial Yards inc. At the time, it was hoped that they could eventually replace all guns that used physical munitions. However, the number of accidents and dangerous internal meltdowns convinced the EAA to shelve the concept of an all-Vent-Cannon ship such as the Gladiator, since it has no other weapons should the core grow unstable. The Resistance has been able to overlook these flaws, given the advantages the class offers. Without physical munitions, it never needs ammunition resupply so can operate offensively more or less indefinitely, providing its cores are maintained. Also, Vent Cannons are especially devastating, if unreliable. Such power is particularly attractive to Kalium – the rogue Colony has produced fully three times the number of this class than were laid-down before the Scourge invasion.
ship.namesake: A [gladiator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladiator), the armed fighter who battled for the crowd's favour in the arenas of ancient Rome.

ship.name: Heavy Cruiser
ship.lore: Designs for Resistance cruisers are widely varied, to the point where listing each variation ever sighted would be as expansive as a list of each individual admiral in the galaxy. As such, it’s best to describe them in general terms, focused more on their capabilities and armaments than form. In this context, a “cruiser” means anything from a Heavy Cruiser to a Light Cruiser, as the UCM would classify them. A further complication is the optional presence of ablative armour panels, adding the classification of “armoured” to the description. Typically, all Resistance cruisers offer respectable survivability, low cost and a broad choice of weaponry. However, their outdated designs do show in poor scan range and limited point defence. Some of these vessels have been adapted from civilian service, generally by adding weapons. Such modified ships often have ablative armour added to overcome their relatively weak designs. Kalium also produces many such low-spec vessels for direct military use, which perform similarly to these adapted ships. This keeps costs low, giving the Kabal numbers to boast over.
ship.rulesText: This ship must take a total of five options from the Cruiser Systems list. A maximum of two options from the Broadside Hardpoint categories may be taken and up to two options may be taken from the Structures category.

variants.name: Kalium KNC-5
variants.note: This Ship counts as a Resistance Light Cruiser with one NC-16 Missile Bank and two Vent Cannon Turrets.
variants.lore:
Generally, Kalium’s ruling Kabal prefers to replicate proven pre-war designs than to innovate, with a focus on numbers. However, after Kalium’s first major blooding in the opening stages of the Battle for Earth, deficiencies became apparent. Visitors to UCM vessels brought back memories (and hushed whispers) that their ships might not be as advanced as their Kabal proclaimed. While combat performance was solid, helped by the iron discipline of their career-sailors, the lack of modern “dressings” in crew areas verged on embarrassing. Clunky 2D viewscreens, general lack of lighting and spartan comforts were more visible than inefficient drives and un-optimised construction.

Kalium’s latest vessels, while essentially the same underneath, have a more modern, distinct appearance as well as countless internal refinements. Kalium still does not favour colourful class names, though. A “KNC-5” (Kalium Navy Cruiser, Type 5) is one of their most common, new line cruisers, armed with a pair of vent cannon turrets and a potent close action missile array.

variants.name: Kalium KNC-12
variants.note: This Ship counts as a Resistance Light Cruiser with one Vent Cannon Turret and two Fighters & Bombers.
variants.lore:
Kalium’s newest vessels’ unique aesthetic suggests a deliberate attempt by the Kabal to “brand” their forces, or at least to make them distinct from the old, tired ships of Resistance fleets. Certainly, the brutalist design speaks of utility, strength and a total disdain for beauty – not that the UCM cares much for those either, but at least they don’t seem to revel in them. The KNC-12 Fleet Carrier is one of the more common, offering excellent, cost-efficient utility to any admiral by way of a potent (if unsafe) vent cannon turret and a double set of launch bays. Unlike the Shaltari, Kalium has no shortage of pilots.

The increasing percentage of these newest vessels in recent engagements speaks of the extreme speed at which the Kabal can build ships – helped, no doubt, by the multitudes under the whip of penal servitude. Their manufacturing capacity is also fearsome, as scattered reports of the class operating under the flag of several Resistance fleets now exist, suggesting that Kalium’s resupply arrangements, as the only manufacturer of old military hardware, have expanded greatly in recent months.

ship.lore: Guy Fawkes (clearly not his real name) is infamous for one thing, blowing battleships to smithereens with massive fire ships. His small, eager crew of plastique-happy privateers are backed by a personal deep-space shipyard kitted out for packing ships with explosives and armouring them enough to survive a one-way charge towards any enemy of any sufficiently flush benefactor. Fawkes prefers old colony ships as candidates, given their cavernous holds. To their creaking frames his engineers affix laughably thick frontal armour plates, having freed up mass by tearing out crew quarters, weapons, spares and anything needed for long-term operations. In combat, Fawkes flies his ship-sized munition personally alongside an insanely loyal, or just insane, skeleton crew. They all jump ship in escape pods at the last possible moment, coordinating with a nearby friendly vessel to collect them so they might do it all again another day. He's currently on Parliament XIII, with no indication he might retire for the quiet life among his explosively gotten gains.
ship.namesake: [Guy Fawkes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Fawkes) (1570-1606), the conspirator caught beneath Parliament with the gunpowder meant to blow it sky-high in 1605. A convert to Catholicism, he fought for Catholic Spain in the Eighty Years' War before joining the plot, in which he was tasked with guarding the gunpowder and lighting the fuse. He avoided the full horror of his execution by hanging, drawing and quartering by breaking his neck in a fall from the gallows. His effigy is still burnt across Britain each year on Bonfire Night.

ship.name: Collins Support Carrier

specialRules.name: Rapid Drop
specialRules.description: This Ship may launch its Assets at any point during its movement

specialRules.name: Wing Support
specialRules.description: Friendly Fighters within 6” of this Ship can be used for Close Protection against any Kinetic weapons (in addition to Close Action and Bomber attacks). When friendly Fighters within 6” of this Ship are used to remove enemy Bombers, each Fighter removes 2 Bombers instead of 1. When friendly Bombers (of any type) within 6” of a Ship with this rule attack, they Saturation Fire when there are 5 or more Bombers in the attack instead of 6.

ship.lore: The Collins is a class of ship designed to serve as part of humanity's exploration fleets over three hundred years ago. These fleets prized self-sufficiency and endurance above all else, two traits the Collins provided by repairing and refuelling the fleet's shuttles and escorts. Following the Scourge's arrival, the Collins swiftly became an important part of Independent Resistance fleets due to its supply of tough fuel haulers and engineering wings. A single Collins can keep entire squadrons of fighters in the air long after they would otherwise have had to return to their motherships, maintaining the fighter screen for both defensive and scouting purposes.
ship.namesake: [Michael Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Collins_(astronaut)) (1930-2021), the Apollo 11 command-module pilot who orbited the Moon alone while his crewmates landed. A United States Air Force test pilot before joining NASA, he first flew in space on Gemini 10 in 1966, becoming the first person to make two spacewalks on a single mission. After leaving NASA he served as the first director of the National Air and Space Museum in Washington.

ship.name: Aldrin Colony Ship

specialRules.name: Descent
specialRules.description:
When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.

A non-Descent Ship that ends its activation in Atmosphere takes D3 damage. Colossal Ships take 2D3 damage instead.

ship.lore: In many cases, the first humans to set foot on one of the UCM’s colonies did so from a bulk lander deployed by an Aldrin class colony ship. These hardy ships formed the vanguard of most expeditions and were deployed when a world looked suitable for habitation or exploitation. Bulk landers were preferred to dropships in those halcyon days, since advanced opposition was unlikely and heavy machinery was always needed planetside. Today, the Aldrin offers the capacity of a troopship in a package the size of a destroyer, possible since these ships were never designed for open warfare so offer additional space. Being below cruiser sized, they can also operate in atmosphere, protecting them from void weapons fire. Built to a standard not seen since the exploration days, they can withstand abuse no modern civilian vessel could survive.
ship.namesake: [Buzz Aldrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buzz_Aldrin) (born 1930), the Apollo 11 lunar-module pilot and the second human to walk on the Moon. Born Edwin Eugene Aldrin Jr., he flew 66 combat missions in F-86 Sabres during the Korean War and earned a doctorate in astronautics from MIT for his work on orbital rendezvous. He had already flown in space on Gemini 12 before the Apollo 11 mission.

ship.name: Armstrong Destroyer

specialRules.name: Rare
specialRules.description: You may only take one Group of this Ship in a Skirmish-sized game, two in a Clash, three in a Battle, and four in a Reconquest.

specialRules.name: Debris Clearance
specialRules.description: Once per game, this Ship may forgo any attacks it may make. If it does, instead of attacking, this Ship may replace a piece of Debris Field within 6” (measuring to the edge of that Debris Field) with a Micrometeor Cloud of approximately the same size in the same location, or remove a piece of Micrometeor Cloud within 6” from the table.

ship.lore: The Armstrong, Aldrin and Collins are some of the earliest human starships still in service; dating back to the late 24th century, they were designed for endurance exploration. Every UCM colony was discovered by hit-and-miss expeditions, requiring many semi-random foldspace jumps until a usable world could be found, explored and given a node. Such dependable hardiness ensured three centuries' service. In size and capability they equal a modern destroyer, though in displacement they are more akin to cruisers due to multiple redundancies, cavernous storage and antique tech. The Armstrong is armed with a deadly HF-6 Clearance Laser which, while useful in the long task of asteroid clearance, is put to much better use against enemy ships, offering Resistance an option for Burnthrough.
ship.namesake: [Neil Armstrong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Armstrong) (1930-2012), commander of Apollo 11 and the first human to set foot on the Moon, in 1969. A naval aviator and test pilot, he flew the X-15 rocket plane before joining NASA and commanded the Gemini 8 mission in 1966. His words on stepping onto the lunar surface, "that's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind", became among the most famous ever spoken.

ship.name: Baleares Pocket Carrier

specialRules.name: Vectored
specialRules.description: This Ship may make an additional turn at any point during its movement, regardless of the Order its Group has taken.

ship.lore: Add a massive engine bank to a set of launch bays and you have the Baleares, a carrier whose strike craft are self-powered. Even today, the Baleares is one of the fastest carriers in mankind’s fleets and embodies the concept of the pre-war pocket carrier. Typically, a carrier will operate beyond line of sight or shielded within the fleet to strike at the enemy’s centre. Since almost nothing can keep pace with the Baleares, it fights quite differently and offers unusual advantages. Baleares captains use their speed to break out from the main fleet, surge forward and launch their daring waves at small, rearguard support vessels. These targets usually offer little point defence, making them vulnerable to strike craft though they are usually beyond their range - not so with the Baleares.
ship.namesake: [The Balearic Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balearic_Islands), whose slingers were prized as deadly skirmishers in the armies of Carthage and Rome. Today the archipelago forms an autonomous community and province of Spain, made up chiefly of Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza and Formentera. Its capital is Palma, and both Catalan and Spanish are official languages.

ship.name: Sagitarii Cutter

specialRules.name: Vectored
specialRules.description: This Ship may make an additional turn at any point during its movement, regardless of the Order its Group has taken.

ship.lore: The Sagittarii is essentially an engine bank with a weapons suite attached to the prow. Extraordinarily fast (especially for a Resistance vessel), almost all the ship’s power is consumed by the drives, necessitating a low power primary armament. Fortunately, pre-war designers still used crude, chemical-based guns and they mounted four of the largest in fixed-forward positions. Though much fatter, the N-12 cannon offers destructive parity with modern medium mass rivers. Built in various configurations over the years, the Sagittarii is a typical pre-war cutter, if ‘typical’ can even be applied to such a specialist ship. Cutters were bulkier and actually more common in the EAA Navy than in the modern UCMF, since speed could compensate for inferior scanning technology in first strike missions. Many escaped the Scourge invasion using that speed and have been valued assets to the Resistance ever since. Kalium’s Kabal appreciate the brutal simplicity of the design, so still manufacture them new in state-run yards.
ship.namesake: The [sagittarii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagittarii), the auxiliary archers who lent ranged firepower to the close-packed ranks of the Roman legions.

When you assign weapons to a Group that has a Telescope token, you may remove the token. If you do, one of the Group's Weapon Systems lowers the result required to score a critical against that Group by 1 for that attack (so a weapon that would crit on a 5+ crits on a 4+ instead).
Telescope tokens placed by this Ship persist between rounds and are only removed when this Ship would place another Telescope token or when a Ship with a Telescope token goes on the Silent Running order.

ship.lore: Galileo orbital telescopes are among the oldest human ships still flying. In the earliest days of foldspace exploration, jumps to un-noded locations had to be conducted in drive-wearing ‘hops’ or random inaccuracy would result. Surveying potential jump locations for potential and celestial threats necessitated a ship built around a gigantic, high-power scanner. Speed was unimportant, so the superstructure of the more common Newton class monitor was chosen as an efficient, low-cost base. Never a military vessel, the Galileo is unarmed besides basic point defence. Surviving Galileos were vital to stranded Resistance fleets forced to use archaic jump-hops to seek the meagre resources not already discovered and either captured by the Scourge or (as with the Colonies) had their node codes changed. Being able to detect enemy activity from a vast distance is also of great use to those small remnant fleets hiding in the cracks of the galaxy - lest they be ambushed. At battlespace level, such observational power can be turned on in-system targets to achieve extraordinary definition unachievable with smaller hardware. This can augment Resistance vessels’ older scanning technology and aid a skilled captain in targeting vulnerable spots on enemy
ship.namesake: [Galileo Galilei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei) (1564-1642), the Italian astronomer whose telescope revealed Jupiter's moons and remade our view of the heavens. Often called the father of modern science, he made pioneering studies of motion and free fall by combining experiment with mathematics. His public defence of the Copernican view that the Earth orbits the Sun led the Roman Inquisition to try him in 1633, after which he spent his last years under house arrest.

specialRules.name: Monitor
specialRules.description: Ships with this rule may not use Course Change or Max Thrust orders.

specialRules.description: Groups with this rule may begin the game Directly Deployed, ignoring the normal Scenario Deployment and Approach Types (though still counting towards Groups Directly Deployed). If it does, it may be deployed up to 4” away from your Deployment Zone.

ship.lore: The Newton was the most common pre-war naval defence monitor in the service of mankind. Unlike modern monitors, the class is visually closer to a space station than a ship, suiting its near- static mission profile. With the speed of the Scourge invasion, few could manoeuvre into a firing position - unfortunate since it packs an enormous mass driver for a frigate-sized vessel. The XN-40 “Godray” was designed to destroy incoming targets long before they could return fire. It sits on a swivel mount, allowing not only tracking of deep space, but precise bombardment of surface targets. Pre-war this was largely used to quell any thoughts of insurrection or to level inhospitable landscape prior to surface exploration. Today, the Newton still brings incredible firepower for its cost, at the price of speed and survivability. This gives it a valued place on the gun line of any Resistance or Kalium admiral capable of harnessing this ship’s strengths. Although unwieldy to bring to a forward position, its bombardment and anti-shipping firepower can lend the class a new lease of life in an offensive role.
ship.namesake: [Sir Isaac Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton) (1642-1727), who set down the laws of motion and gravitation that govern every ship's course. His Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica, published in 1687, is among the most important works in the history of science. He also built the first reflecting telescope, showed that white light is a mixture of colours, and shares credit with Leibniz for the development of calculus. In later life he served as Master of the Royal Mint and President of the Royal Society.

ship.name: Heavy Frigate

specialRules.name: Reinforced Armour
specialRules.description: Weapons rolling to hit this Ship or its Group can only score criticals against it on a result of a 3 higher than its Lock value.

ship.lore: As with cruisers, the sheer variety of frigate designs in service with the Resistance is staggering. Similarly, it’s best to discuss them in terms of capability and armament. Many of these ships were originally civilian-grade, but have since had weapons added in response to dire need. All Resistance frigates are faster than cruisers, offering a first strike/ flanking option. They are often used to seek and destroy key enemy vessels early in an engagement, to protect the larger ships in the fleet. Their weapons basically define their role and mode of attack, be that aggressive close-action or standoff fire. In this context, the term “frigate” also encompasses Strike Carriers and unarmed Electronic Warfare Ships. A common pre-war practice was the production of Heavy Frigates, heavily armoured often with two main weapon systems. These have fallen out of favour with the UCMF due to high cost and the drain of dual weapons systems on engine power.

specialRules.description: When this ship is destroyed, it explodes with a range of 3” and rolls 1D3 on the Explosion Effect table.

ship.lore: Though lacking in military resources, most fleets scattered by the Scourge invasion had a high proportion of merchantmen - rightly more likely to run than engage. Forced to be inventive, ragtag Resistance groups sought to repurpose civilian vessels to military ends. Haulers often make poor gun platforms but offer capacious internal holds. When combined with ‘repurposed’ shuttles, yachts and small transports, a formidable weapon can result: the Detonator, a hive of remote-operated, explosive-packed fire ships. The most common vessel is a Seneca class - unweildy and utilitarian, it offered pre-war traders the largest storage for the lowest cost, although many other patterns are in service in this unlikely role. Crewing a repurposed flimsy brick fizzing with improvised time bombs is not for the sane and/or skittish. These individuals are treated with wary respect when on shore leave, notable in the bar due to singed hair - if they’ve survived to douse their burns in booze. In the service of Kalium, Detonators are employed in an altogether more sinister, regimented fashion, which says a lot of how much the Kabal values flesh and blood.
ship.namesake: [Seneca the Younger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seneca_the_Younger) (c.4 BC-AD 65), the Roman Stoic philosopher and statesman, tutor to Nero and forced to take his own life. Born in Corduba in Roman Spain, he was one of the foremost writers of Stoic philosophy, best known for his moral essays and his Letters to Lucilius. He also wrote nine tragedies, including Medea and Thyestes, which strongly influenced Renaissance and Elizabethan drama.
